short_description: Moderate = 2.2mi/3.54km total; 219ft/67m elevation gain; 2-3 hours. The trail leads you via ladders, steps, and ropes to a rocky beach, where you can enjoy the sound of the waves and take in the Western view of Pola Island.

title: Mount Alava Trail
accessibility: Due to being steep, slippery, and rocky this trail not considered accessible.
short_description: Difficult = 7mi/11.27km total; 1,607ft/490m elevation gain; 4-5 hours. Trail can be steep, slippery, and rocky in places. Stunning panoramic views from the summit. Lush rainforest environment, great for bird and fruit bat watching.

title: Seasonal Programs and Special Events
accessibility: Due to the nature of the park's location on mountainous terrain, visitors will encounter changes in grade, uneven pathways and gravel paths. There are some accessible locations in the park though the path of travel to the location may not be accessible. Please call ahead for more information or seek the assistance of a ranger at the start of your visit.
short_description: Each season brings a variety of unique program and special event opportunities. Find out what opportunities are available during your visit!

title: Swimming
accessibility: Beach wheelchairs available at the visitor center, first come, first served.
short_description: Splashing in the surf and bodyboarding are a favorite activity along the beach.

title: Hanford: Attend a B Reactor Tour
topics: African American Heritage;Cold War;World War II
accessibility: On the Department of Energy B Reactor tour, visitors must be able to walk short distances on uneven surfaces and sit in a passenger bus for 45 minutes at a time. The Department of Energy offers wheelchair accessible buses and sign language interpretation for these tours by request. Requests must be made at least two weeks in advance by emailing B Reactor tours or calling 509-376-1647. Additional accessibility features are available in the B Reactor including: 3-D Tactile Map: Covering the B Reactor tour path, the 3-D tactile map is primarily designed for blind and partially sighted users to gain a spatial understanding of the B Reactor. The map is available upon request at the visitor center for use on the B Reactor tours. Audio Description Tour of the B Reactor: This feature is available through the NPS app under my settings. Tour is designed to assist blind and low vision visitors with navigating and experiencing the B Reactor while on a public tour. Exhibit Panel Descriptions: Text and descriptions of each exhibit panel in the Atomic Culture Room , Health Physics Room , and History Room within the B Reactor are available on the park website. Braille is available for the Haiku for You magnetic word interactive exhibit.
short_description: The US Department of Energy provides guided tours of the B Reactor. These tours provide a glimpse into the science and technology that made plutonium production possible on an industrial scale and helped launch the nuclear age.

title: Multi-Park Loop
topics: American Revolution;Architecture and Building;Colonization and Settlement;Explorers and Expeditions;Forests and Woodlands;Deciduous Forests;Landscape Design;Military;Infantry and Militia;US Air Force (Army Air Corps);US Army;US Marines;US Navy;Monuments and Memorials;Native American Heritage;Natural Sounds;Presidents;River and Riparian;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Trails;Water Trails;Transportation;Bridges;Canals;Roads, Routes and Highways;Tunnels;Urban America;Wars and Conflicts;American Revolutionary War;Civil War;Colonial/European Contact Conflicts;Korean War;Spanish-American War;Vietnam War;War of 1812;World War I;World War II;Waterfalls;Watersheds
accessibility: The Normanstone Trail, Whitehaven Trail, and Glover-Archbold Park Trail can be muddy, rugged, and narrow. These trails are not recommended for those who experience difficulty moving over rough terrain. Anyone wanting to attempt this hike can alter it to suit their needs by proceeding through Georgetown and remaining on sidewalks to get to Dumbarton Oaks Park and Montrose Park. Proceeding along city streets will provide visitors with the opportunity to view the architecture of Georgetown homes. The C&O Canal, Mount Vernon Trail and the National Mall are accessible.
short_description: Park your car and stretch your legs! Visit four different National Parks in Washington, DC and begin logging miles on seven different National Historic or National Scenic trails!

title: Nike Missile Site in the Marin Headlands
accessibility: Nike Missile Site Accessibility There are usable parking available one site. The area is paved and generally flat, but is not striped. There is an accessible portable toilet available in the front of the parking area. All tours are guided by a park employee, docent, or volunteer. These individuals will tailor the tours to the needs of the visitors. ASL interpreters are available on request, with 5 days advanced notice. All the buildings are generally accessible to visitors with mobility disabilities. Some portions of the buildings do not provide adequate turning space for visitors who use wheelchairs. There are two military trailers that are not accessible to visitors who use wheelchairs. The trailers are extremely compact. However, visitors are able to view inside from the entry doors. Some routes throughout the site contain cross slopes greater than 2.08% and changes in level that exceed 1/4". The route leading to the Generator building has a running slope of 7.5%, proceed with caution. Some of the exhibits are tactile, including a scale replica of the missile. There are accessible picnic tables on site. Audio described and open caption videos are available on our website .
short_description: Visit and explore a Nike Missile site and learn about the role of the military installations here in the Marin Headlands.

title: Rent a Bicycle
topics: American Revolution;Forts;Monuments and Memorials;Scenic Views;American Revolutionary War;Women's History
fee_description: Rental Prices (Fees do not include sales tax) Adult Pedal Bikes: $20 for one hour / $35 for 2 hours / $45 for 3 hours / $55 all day Electric E-Bikes (must be 16 years of age to ride with guardian and 18 years of age to ride solo: $25 for one hour / $45 for 2 hours / $55 for 3 hours / $65 all day Child Bikes and Trailers: $10 for one hour / $15 for 2 hours / $20 for 3 hours / $30 all day
accessibility: The most popular route for riding bicycles is the paved Joseph Plumb Martin trail. The trail is wide and most sections are fairly flat, but there are also some steeper grades that may not be accessible for some users.
short_description: For those who want to explore Valley Forge on two wheels, The Encampment Store offers seasonal bike rentals, weather permitting. Please call 610-551-7870 before going to the park to confirm that bike rentals are on for the day.

title: Grassy Lake Road
fee_description: Accessing the road from north or south requires paying the park fee for Grand Teton or Yellowstone.
accessibility: Use caution on this dirt road. High clearance vehicles are recommended, and the road is closed for grizzly bear migration until June 1. Sections of the road may open later depending on conditions.
short_description: Grassy Lake Road is a dirt road connecting Flagg Ranch to Ashton, Idaho.

title: Cave Tours
fee_description: Fees vary for each cave tour. Visit the park website for a full list of park fees .
accessibility: The difficulty of cave tours vary from easy, moderate, or difficult. Most tours include paved walking trails. Many of the tours also include several hundred stair steps. Service animals are welcome. More information about accessibility in the park is available.
short_description: Join a ranger as you discover the complex history and intricate geology of the worlds longest cave system.

title: Parked at Home
topics: African American Heritage;Arts;Asian American Heritage;Commerce;Trade;Dams;Engineering;Enslavement;Farming and Agriculture;Hispanic American Heritage;Immigration;Industry;Factories;Mills;Mining;LGB American Heritage;Laborer and Worker;Labor Movement;Migrant Workers;Latino American Heritage;Maritime;Military;Monuments and Memorials;Native American Heritage;Pacific Islander Heritage;Reconstruction;Religion and Spirituality;River and Riparian;Science, Technology and Innovation;Social Movements;Urban America;World War II;Westward Expansion;The Gold Rush;Women's History
accessibility: An American Sign Language (ASL) Interpreter will provide signing services for all 6 programs. If you have any questions or concerns about accessibility, please contact Ranger Mark Mello
short_description: Explore America's national parks from the comfort of home. Every park has a story. During this virtual series, we’ll connect with people from across the country to talk about special places and complex stories at National Park Service sites. Join us to learn more about a place that might be close to home, or in a destination you dream of visiting. Each hour-long program includes a presentation and opportunities for questions and answers.

title: Round Spring Guided Cave Tour
fee_description: Current prices are as follows: $10 for adults $5 for children (12 and under) $5 for adults with a qualifying Access or Senior Pass
accessibility: Due to stairs and the natural terrain of the cave, these tours are not accessible to wheelchairs and may be difficult for those with mobility impairments. Stooping for a moderate distance is required to enter the cave, and gravel or mud may prove difficult to navigate once inside. Service animals are allowed, given that they meet the requirements outlined by NPS policy . In short, service animals "must be trained to perform a specific task related to the disability of its handler." "Emotional support" or "comfort" animals do not qualify as service animals for the sake of this policy.
short_description: Discover the amazing world beneath your feet! Round Spring Cave is considered the most spectacular cave within Ozark National Scenic Riverways. Large, varied formations fill over a mile of the passage, which has been well-preserved over the years. There is no better way to learn about Ozark caves than through a tour!

title: Mount Rainier: Off the Beaten Path
topics: Architecture and Building;Forests and Woodlands;Geology;Glaciers;Lakes;Landscape Design;Mountains;River and Riparian;Scenic Views;Trails;Roads, Routes and Highways;Volcanoes;Waterfalls;Wilderness
fee_description: Park entrance fee is required.
accessibility: Park roads are narrow, steep, and winding and do not have shoulders. Parking areas are usually paved unless stated otherwise (such as on Westside Road). Trails are dirt, often broken by tree roots, log or rock steps, and can have significant elevation gains and losses.
short_description: Mount Rainier National Park is substantial in size, but congestion still occurs during peak season and during times of nice weather. Escaping the crowds completely can be a challenge, but there are ways to still plan a rewarding visit. This guide provides alternatives to popular locations like Paradise and Sunrise. However, the secret is out! Even relatively less popular areas can still be busy.

title: Hike the Lake View Trail
fee_description: The Lakeview Trail is in a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: This trail is an unmaintained route. It is 4.7 miles (7.6 km) roundtrip on some uneven rocks, gravel, and loose sand. There is about 115 feet of elevation change with steep inclines/declines throughout the trail.
short_description: Lakeview hiking trail allows visitors to explore the beautiful mountainous landscape and the desert flora and fauna including creosote, brittle bush.

title: Park Films in the South Rim Visitor Center Theater
fee_description: Admission is free and performances are open to the public.
accessibility: The theater is located inside the Grand Canyon Visitor Center, which is wheelchair accessible. Park Rangers are available at the information desk for questions. Wheelchairs and tandem bicycles are available for rent at Canyon Adventures Bike Rental and Cafe, next to the visitor center; (928) 599-1011 or bikegrandcanyon.com. During film showings: Open captioning is used in all showings
short_description: Park Films Are Shown Daily in the Visitor Center Theater. ►At the top of the hour, the 24-minute film, ‘We Are Grand Canyon’, welcomes visitors by sharing the heritage and viewpoints of the 11 tribal communities connected to the canyon. ►On the half hour, 'Grand Canyon - a Journey of Wonder', introduces the natural and human history of this special place —along with efforts to preserve and protect Grand Canyon as a sanctuary for plants, animals, and humans.

title: Visit the White Haven Home
accessibility: The historic White Haven estate and adjacent outbuildings are approximately 400 feet up a gradual incline from the visitor center. An accessible entrance into White Haven for wheelchairs, walkers, and other mobility devices is available on the eastern side of the home, roughly 100 yards from the Visitor Center. All but one room on the main floor of the house is wheelchair accessible. The historic Winter Kitchen in the basement of the house is only accessible by stairs. Park staff can provide a binder with photographs and interpretive text from the winter kitchen upon request. All outbuildings are accessible. Assistive Listening Devices (ALDs) are available for guided house tours upon request, and a short film presentation in the historic dining room features an induction loop for visitors with T-coil enabled hearing aids.
short_description: The historic White Haven estate is more than 200 years old and the home where Ulysses and Julia Grant fell in love. The house is open daily from 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

title: Bike the Potomac Heritage National Scenic Trail in Prince William Forest Park
topics: Fire;Forests and Woodlands;Natural Sounds;River and Riparian;Trails;Transportation;Roads, Routes and Highways;Watersheds
fee_description: Standard Entrance Pass is $20.00 for Private Vehicles, Motorcycle are $15.00, and Per Person is $10.00
accessibility: The Scenic Drive is a paved road with several steep grades and blind curves for the first two miles. Burma Road is a 1.4 mi (2.3km) crushed rock road. There is a nice gentle descent down to a bridge crossing which is followed by the climbs and descends to the gate at the Park Boundary. The roundtrip distance is about 10 miles (16 kilometers) with 900 feet (274 meters) of elevation gain/loss.
short_description: Discover Northern Virginia's best kept secret and bike along the park’s Scenic Drive.

title: Tour Independence Hall
topics: African American Heritage;American Revolution;Enslavement;Jails and Prisons;American Revolutionary War
fee_description: Admission to Independence is free.
accessibility: The first floor of Independence Hall is accessible for those with mobility impairments. For those with hearing impairments, the "Birthplace of a Nation" pamphlet provides written information about the rooms shown on the tour. Ask a ranger for an assistive listening device or an audio described tour. American Sign Language interpretation is available by request. You must call the park to arrange for an interpreter at least 14 days prior to your visit. Get the details on how to reserve an ASL interpreter here.
short_description: Take a ranger-led tour of the birthplace of the United States. Hear stories of conflict, compromise, and the complicated business of making a nation.

title: Visit the Jean Baptiste Vallé House
accessibility: There are seven steps to enter the Jean Baptiste Vallé House.
short_description: Built in 1794, the Jean Baptiste Vallé House was home to the last Commandant of Ste. Genevieve. Jean Baptiste Vallé oversaw the transition from colonial town to a part of the United States after the Louisiana Purchase. The grounds are open daily from dawn to dusk. Join a ranger-led program to visit the building's interior and learn more about the history of the house and its residents.

title: Visit the Bauvais-Amoureux House
topics: African American Heritage;Architecture and Building;Colonization and Settlement;Enslavement;Civil Rights;Women's History
accessibility: There are 7 steps with a handrail to enter the main floor of the home. There is a flagstone path with two steps leading to the basement entrance. Currently, the home is not wheelchair accessible. The home's entrance is about 50 feet across a mostly-level, mowed lawn from the gravel parking area. For up-to-date accessibility information, please inquire at the Welcome Center or call 573-880-7189.
short_description: Built in 1792, the Bauvais-Amoureux House stands as an architectural gem with a rich past. Here, Pélagie Amoureux, a woman who was formerly enslaved, and her husband Benjamin, a Frenchman, raised their family. The grounds are open from dawn to dusk, and the building is open daily for self-guided visits. Join a ranger-led program to learn more about the history of the house and its residents.

title: Visit Green Tree Tavern
topics: African American Heritage;Architecture and Building;Colonization and Settlement;Commerce;Enslavement;Westward Expansion
accessibility: There are eight steps with no handrail to reach the grounds of Green Tree Tavern. After crossing a mowed lawn, there are an additional nine steps with handrails to reach the entrance of Green Tree Tavern. Currently, the home is not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: As the oldest building still standing in Ste. Genevieve, Green Tree Tavern has had a rich history. It has served as a home, a business, and a Masonic Lodge over the years. The grounds are open from dawn to dusk, and the building is open daily for self-guided visits. Join a ranger-led program to learn more about the history of the house and its residents.

title: Snowmobile in Kenai Fjords National Park
accessibility: There is no running water at this time of year. There are pit toilets available. The road conditions will depend on how much snow has fallen. The main trail to the Exit Glacier Area is on a two lane road that has been closed to vehicle traffic.
short_description: Explore Kenai Fjords National Park by snowmobile. Once the road to Exit Glacier is snow-covered and closed to cars, it is accessible by snowmobile,

title: Become a Jean Lafitte B.A.R.K. Ranger
accessibility: To learn about accessibility at each of our park sites, visit our accessibility page . Service Animals are welcome to join this program.
short_description: Hey dog! Do you want to explore parts of Jean Lafitte National Historical Park and Preserve with your leash-holding companions? Interested in getting your very own B.A.R.K. Ranger dog tag? We made it easy for your human to help you get one. Just follow the B.A.R.K. Ranger code!

title: Learn about the Johnstown Flood in the Visitor Center
fee_description: There are no fees for entrance or public activities at Johnstown Flood National Memorial.
accessibility: There are designated accessible parking spots in the parking lot. The walkway to the Visitor Center and the building itself is handicap accessible. An elevator is located on the upper level. Handicap accessible seating is located at the top of the Visitor Center theater. A wheel chair is available for use. The park film "Black Friday" and the Victor Heiser exhibit contain captions that are visible during every showing. A transcript of the park film is available at the Visitor Center desk. Braille versions of the park brochure are available at the Visitor Center desk. Service animals are welcome.
short_description: The Visitor Center and has two floors of exhibits and a park film. Visitors will learn about the Johnstown Flood of May 31, 1889.

title: Ranger-led Programs at Padre Island
topics: Animals;Archeology;Climate Change;Dunes;Estuaries and Mangroves;Ranches;Geology;Prairies;Ships and Shipwrecks;US Navy;Native American Heritage;Scenic Views;Endangered;World War II;Wetlands
fee_description: All programs are offered free of charge. However, there is a fee to enter the park.
accessibility: Programs are suitable for all ages. Beach wheelchairs are available at the visitor center, first come, first served. Some programs such as Beach Walk, Cowboys and Caracaras, Learn to Surf Fish, and Tranquil Tides requires walking on uneven terrain. Sunrise Yoga takes place on the Malaquite Visitor Center rooftop deck. The rooftop is accessed by two flights of stairs.
short_description: Discover Padre Island National Seashore with free ranger-led programs like beach walks and deck talks! Explore nature, history, and wildlife while enjoying the Gulf shoreline or chatting over coffee with a ranger. Check the NPS App or visitor center for schedules and pop-up events.

title: Become a Padre Island Junior Ranger
accessibility: The Junior Ranger program is open to all ages and abilities.
short_description: Are you interested in exploring? Would you like to learn more about the national parks that belong to you? Do you want to learn how you can help protect these special places? If so, become a Padre Island Junior Ranger! The Junior Ranger activity books are appropriate for all ages and are a great way to learn about the natural wonders of the national seashore.

title: Check-out a Junior Ranger Discovery Pack
accessibility: Junior Ranger Discovery Packs are available for check out on a first come, first served basis. There is no charge to check out a pack.
short_description: Families and groups with children can borrow a free Discovery Pack from the Malaquite Visitor Center to explore Padre Island. Each pack includes an activity guide, field guides, binoculars, magnifiers, and more.

title: Walk the Moments in Time Trail
accessibility: The Moments in Time Trail has a hard-packed surface and some uneven surfaces from tree roots and other obstacles. It has an elevation gain of about 9 feet. Service animals are allowed. Service animals may accompany their owner to all park locations. Under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Service animals are defined as dogs that are individually trained to do work or perform tasks for people with disabilities. Dogs whose sole function is to provide comfort or emotional support do not qualify as service animals under the ADA.
short_description: Take a peaceful stroll at Barnes Point on Lake Crescent on the Moments in Time Trail.

title: Take Me Fishing
accessibility: This is an outdoor program. Individuals must travel about 100 yards from the parking lot to arrive at the structure where this program is hosted. Individuals will have to walk along a crushed gravel path. This service is stable, but can get muddy if it has recently rained. Chairs and seating are available in the barn space. A portable toilet is available adjacent to the barn.
short_description: Learn to fish with us this summer! Join park staff Sunday afternoons in June, July, and August for some FREE family fun. Catch some fish, learn about the river, and earn a Junior Angler badge. All fishing material and bait are provided. Activities available from 11:00 AM - 4:00 PM.

title: Nature Walk and Scavenger Hunt
accessibility: This program is outside with no seating available. Participants should be able to walk up to a mile and stand on their feet for at least an hour. Paths are mostly gravel and dirt and might be difficult to access with a wheelchair.
short_description: Join us for nature walk and scavenger hunt. These walks through the Blackstone River State Park are intended for naturalists of all ages. Younger visitors will be able to complete a plant and animal scavenger hunt. Binoculars and animal identification guides are available for participants to borrow.

title: Towpath Talk
topics: Animals;Climate Change;Commerce;Dams;Engineering;Farming and Agriculture;Geology;Immigration;Industry;Factories;Mills;Laborer and Worker;Labor Movement;Natural Sounds;River and Riparian;Scenic Views;Transportation;Bridges;Canals;Roads, Routes and Highways;Trains and Railroads;Waterfalls;Watersheds
accessibility: The towpath with composed of stone and dirt. It is a relatively flat path but can be muddy depending on the season. Wheelchairs might have difficulty moving across the unpaved surfaces. Folks should wear closed toed, well-fitting shoes. Participants will be expected to remain on their feet for the entire duration of the program. Limited access to restroom facilities at the site. Water is highly recommended.
short_description: Join a Park Ranger for guided walk along the historic Blackstone Canal. This program is offered on Saturdays in the months of June, July, and August.

title: Places of Interest Related to Carter G. Woodson
topics: African American Heritage;Architecture and Building;Great Depression;Migrations;Monuments and Memorials;Reconstruction;Religion and Spirituality;Schools and Education;Social Movements;Civil Rights;Voting Rights and Suffrage;Urban America;Wars and Conflicts;American Revolutionary War;Civil War;World War I;World War II
accessibility: Service animals are allowed
short_description: After you visit the Carter G. Woodson Home National Historic Site, check out these nearby places.

title: Skiing and Snowshoeing the C&O Canal Towpath
fee_description: No fee will be collected unless parking at the Great Falls Tavern Visitor Center.
accessibility: Plan Ahead and Prepare We recommend planning your trip in advance, preparing for various weather and trail conditions, and practicing common trail etiquette to create a safe and enjoyable trip. Safety Regulations The speed limit on the towpath is 15 miles per hour. Please travel single file and stay to the right. Give an audible signal when passing, pass on the left, and only when it is safe to do so. Wheelchairs Wheelchairs and similar devices built specifically for mobility disabilities are allowed on the towpath. The towpath is a flat, gravel path.
short_description: During the winter months, the C&O Canal may accumulate enough snow for winter activities like skiing and snowshoeing. Visitors can step out onto the towpath and enjoy a short or multi-mile journey along the historic canal

title: Scramble down Cathedral Wash Trail
accessibility: Steep trail descends multiple times onto uneven rock surface. Not recomended for anyone without rock canyon experience. No flat surfaces, no railings. Rock scrabbles, narrow ledges, soft sand and puddles found along the trail leading to a soft sand riverbank.
short_description: Follow Cathedral Wash trail as it climbs down to meet the Colorado River on its sandy bank. The 3 miles (4.8 km) round-trip challenging hike descend into the rocky wash, traveling through the Kaibab Limestone and Toroweap Formations of the Grand Canyon Group. Some rock scrambling required.

title: From Your Boat To The Bridge
topics: Canyons and Canyonlands;Geology;Native American Heritage;Natural Sounds;Rock Landscapes and Features;Arches;Scenic Views;Trails
fee_description: Rainbow Bridge has no entrance fee. You will be traveling through Glen Canyon National Recreation Area to get to Rainbow Bridge, which does charge an entrance fee. Rainbow Bridge is only accessible from Glen Canyon by boat, so if you do not have a boat of your own, you will most likely have to rent a boat or take a boat tour.
accessibility: The trail is a combination of boat dock, mud, concrete, packed dirt, loose dirt, rocks, and some uphill/downhill walking. It is not recommended for people with low mobility. Service animals are permitted on the trail only. The trail length changes throughout the year, all dependent on water levels. It is always at least 1 mile one-way. If water levels are low, traversing up and down the bank and crossing a shallow creek may be required to reach the main trail. Soft sandy soil and muddy creek beds may be present. If water levels are high, the main trail is hard pack dirt/sand with sections of varying elevation gain and slick rock sandstone.
short_description: There is one designated trail within the boundaries of Rainbow Bridge National Monument. It runs the length of the monument, from the boat dock on one side, to the border with the Navajo Nation on the other. We ask that you stay on this trail when you visit Rainbow Bridge for your safety and out of respect for the local Native American tribes that hold this place special to them.

title: Explore the National A. Philip Randolph Pullman Porter Museum
topics: African American Heritage;Industry;Laborer and Worker;Labor Movement;Social Movements;Civil Rights;Transportation;Trains and Railroads
fee_description: Go to https://aprpullmanportermuseum.org/ for current fees. As of fall 2020, fees are $5.00 per person.
accessibility: Handicap accessible ramp and elevator available.
short_description: This important museum details the struggle of African Americans in the Pullman Company to obtain representation and rights, and the role of A. Philip Randolph, chief organizer of what eventually became the Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters.

title: Take a Self-Guided Tour of Pullman
topics: African American Heritage;Architecture and Building;Industry;Factories;Laborer and Worker;Labor Movement;Social Movements;Trains and Railroads
accessibility: This tour can be taken by foot or by driving. The city streets and sidewalks offer wheelchair accesibility/ramps. Handicap parking spaces are available at the visitor center.
short_description: Our partner, the Friends of Pullman National Historical Park, offers a free self-guided walking/driving tour pamphlet. It is available at the Pullman Exhibit Hall and the Administration-Clock Tower Building. The Pullman Exhibit Hall also has a brochure box with the tour map available at its entrance door on the outside of the building.

title: Winter Programs
topics: Animals;Birds;Climate Change;Forests and Woodlands;Geology;Natural Sounds;River and Riparian;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Trails
accessibility: There are differing levels of physical accessibility for these programs. Please reach out to Park Ranger Allison Horrocks if you have any questions in regards to program accessibility.
short_description: Just because it's winter, doesn't mean there's nothing to see and do in the Blackstone River Valley. Check out these awesome programs to learn more about the Valley's geology, birds, and more

title: Guided Tours of Bent's Old Fort
topics: African American Heritage;Architecture and Building;Commerce;Trade;Enslavement;Explorers and Expeditions;Forts;Grasslands;Prairies;Hispanic American Heritage;Laborer and Worker;Latino American Heritage;Military;Native American Heritage;Scenic Views;Trails;Transportation;Roads, Routes and Highways;Wars and Conflicts;Mexican War;Westward Expansion
accessibility: Parking and Wheelchair Use Accessibility parking is available at the visitor parking lot. There is a paved pathway, 1,275 feet in length, from the parking lot to the fort that is hard-surfaced and wheelchair accessible. Fort Accessibility Most of the first floor of the fort is wheelchair accessible, with soft surfaces. Visitors with accessibility needs are asked to arrive thirty minutes in advance or contact the park to arrange accomodations, if needed. Service Animals Service animals are allowed anywhere in the park when kept 25 yards or more away from fort livestock.
short_description: Take a tour with a Park Ranger to learn more about Bent's Old Fort. Tours are limited to fifteen participants and will explore the historic use of the site and the reconstruction of the fort in the 1970s.

accessibility: This unpaved, natural surface trail is approximately 18 inches wide. Service animals are permitted.
short_description: The Valle Grande Exploration Trail (formerly known as the Pond Trail) is a gentle, 0.8-mile round-trip hike to a pond in the heart of Valle Grande. It takes approximately 1 hour to complete. Pets are not permitted.

fee_description: As of January 1, 2025, a park entrance fee is required to enter Valles Caldera National Preserve.
accessibility: This is a narrow, unpaved, natural surface trail with somewhat steep grades.
short_description: The South Valle Grande Trail is a 2-mile round-trip hike that descends to the edge of Valle Grande, offering excellent wildlife viewing opportunities. The hike takes 1-2 hours. Leashed pets are permitted.

title: Hike the South Mountain Trail

accessibility: This unpaved, natural surface trail is steep and narrow. Service animals permitted.
short_description: The South Mountain Trail is an 8.2-mile round-trip hike that climbs to the summit of South Mountain. The hike takes 4-5 hours to complete. Pets are not permitted.

title: Hike the Rabbit Ridge Trail
topics: Animals;Birds;Cats (wild);Elk;Climate Change;Fire;Foothills, Plains and Valleys;Forests and Woodlands;Coniferous Forests;Deciduous Forests;Grasslands;Meadows;Mountains;Night Sky;Astronomy;Scenic Views;Trails;Volcanoes

accessibility: This trail follows old logging routes and traverses steep grades.

accessibility: This trail follows old logging routes and traverses steep grades.
short_description: The Rabbit Mountain Loop (2.9 miles, 4.7 km round-trip), formerly known as the Coyote Call Trail, contours along the southern rim of the caldera, offering great views of Valle Grande and Redondo Peak. The loop takes 1-2 hours. Leashed pets are permitted.

fee_description: As of January 1, 2025, a park entrance fee is required to enter Valles Caldera National Preserve.

short_description: The Jemez River Trail (formerly Hidden Valley Trail) is a 3.4-mile round-trip hike into a picturesque canyon along the East Fork Jemez River. The hike takes 1-2 hours. Pets are not permitted.

topics: Ancient Seas;Animals;Birds;Elk;Archeology;Climate Change;Fire;Foothills, Plains and Valleys;Forests and Woodlands;Coniferous Forests;Geology;Grasslands;Meadows;Prairies;Mountains;Native American Heritage;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Trails;Volcanoes;Headwaters;Wetlands

accessibility: This unpaved, natural surface trail is approximately 18 inches wide. Over 1.5 miles, the elevation range is between 8497 and 8545 feet.
short_description: The Cerro La Jara Loop is a gentle, 1.4-mile hike around Valles Caldera's smallest and youngest volcanic dome. The hike takes approximately 1 hour. Leashed pets are permitted.

title: See the Angus Show Cattle
accessibility: The pathway to the show barn is a several hundred yards at a slight grade and a gravel road, so it may be difficult for persons with mobility issues or those who use a wheelchair.
short_description: A black Angus cattle herd still pasture in the fields once grazed by Eisenhower's own show herd. Visitors to the Eisenhower farm were often treated to a farm tour complete with Eisenhower showing off his pride and joy, the show cattle and show barn.

title: Bunsen Peak Road Ski Trail
fee_description: No fees are required, however, one-way or round-trip skier shuttles may be offered for this trail.
accessibility: This skier-tracked trail follows a mostly flat dirt road for the first three miles when accessed from the trailhead on Swan Lake Flats. The section accessed from the YCC Camp is most difficult due to icy curves and steep downhill sections. Total elevation gain/loss for the trail is 1120 feet. Service dogs allowed with backcountry access permit.
short_description: The Bunsen Peak Road Ski Trail is a one-way skier-tracked easiest to most-difficult trail with two trailhead options. This ski affords views of Swan Lake Flats, the Gardner Canyon, and the Gallatin Mountains.

title: Snow Pass Ski Trail
fee_description: No fees are required, however, one-way or round-trip skier shuttles may be offered for this trail.
accessibility: This skier-tracked trail provides fairly level terrain for the first 2.2 miles (3.5 km) when accessed from the Glen Creek Trailhead on Swan Lake Flats. The section accessed from the Upper Terrace Loop Ski Trail and Mammoth-Norris Road is most difficult due to icy curves and steep downhill sections when traveled from the Glen Creek Trail toward the Upper Terrace Loop Ski Trail or the Mammoth-Norris Road trailheads. Total elevation gain/loss for the trail is 700 feet. Service dogs allowed with backcountry access permit.
short_description: The Snow Pass Ski Trail is a 4.2 mile (6.76 km), skier-tracked, one-way, easiest to most-difficult, ski that takes skiers through a steep heavily forested area to a semi-flat wide open area with views of Swan Lake Flats.

title: Visit Old Slater Mill National Historic Landmark
topics: Architecture and Building;Arts;Birthplace;Commerce;Dams;Engineering;Immigration;Industry;Factories;Mills;Laborer and Worker;Scenic Views;Urban America
accessibility: The mill is fully accessible to individuals with mobility difficulty. However, the structure is a old textile mill. The floors are at times uneven and the space could be difficult to navigate with a wheelchair. The front door is handicap accessible, but the belltower door is not. Individuals requiring a handicapped accessible door should enter through the front door.
short_description: The birthplace of the American Industrial Revolution, Old Slater Mill is open as a museum. Visitors can learn about the history of the site through exhibits, films, and tours. The grounds are open from dawn to dusk. Visitors can read interpretative panels spread across the grounds which help tell the story of the site. Check out the Park's calendar for operating hours and seasons.

title: Hiking with Traction Devices
accessibility: During the winter and spring seasons, from late October to early June, expect conditions on trails to vary. Factors like elevation and access to direct sunlight have an impact on the amount of snow or ice that might be on a trail. During the winter and spring seasons, most trails in Rocky Mountain National Park are covered with snow and ice. Traction devices are helpful when hiking on hard-packed snow and ice. For soft and deeper snow, it is best to switch to snowshoes.
short_description: Enjoy the winter wonderland that Rocky has to offer from late October to early June. When there is hard-packed snow and ice on the trails, don't forget to use traction devices!

title: Old North Church: Prince's Pet Pursuit Family Activity
fee_description: This activity is included with your admission ticket! To participate, simply request a copy of Prince’s Pew Pursuit when you enter the church.
accessibility: Old North's sanctuary is accessible. Note: To avoid steps in the courtyard while following the Freedom Trail from downtown, you will have to make a left at Unity St., take the right on to Tileston St., then make a right on to Salem St.
short_description: Explore Old North through a scavenger hunt narrated by Prince, the friendly North End cat who used to frequent the church.

title: Old North Church: Crypt Tour
topics: American Revolution;Architecture and Building;Burial, Cemetery and Gravesite
fee_description: Visitors may purchase the Crypt Combo package during normal operating hours. The Crypt Combo is $9 per person when you book online, or $10 at the ticket booth. It includes a self-guided tour of the crypt, general admission to the church’s sanctuary and new exhibit, and an immersive audio guide with 300 years of the church’s secrets and stories. Children 5 and under are free. Visit Old North's online schedule to plan your visit.
accessibility: Participants should be comfortable in a basement setting and navigating tight spaces. The crypt has low lighting, uneven surfaces, and is not wheelchair or stroller accessible.
short_description: Take a self-guided tour of Old North’s historic crypt, where 1,100 people were laid to rest.

title: Lower Sauma Ridge Trail
accessibility: One scenic overlook (Lower Sauma Ridge) is accessible with assistance. No other pullouts or overlooks have been developed at this time and trails are unimproved, steep, and rugged.
short_description: Easy = 0.4mi/0.64km total; 232ft/7m elevation gain; 30-45 minutes. A gentle climb to an archaeological site featuring ancient grinding stones, this trail combines history with incredible views of the northeast coastline and the Vai’ava Strait.

title: Pola Island Trail
accessibility: Even though the easiest trail in terms of elevation and distance, due to uneven surface this trail isn't necessarily accessible.
short_description: Easy = 0.1mi/0.16km total; 30ft/9m elevation gain; 15-30 minutes. This short, easy trail leads you to the untouched shores of the South Pacific; delivering big rewards with views of the rugged coastline and Pola Island, a sanctuary for nesting seabirds.

title: Hike Spectacle Island's Drumlins
accessibility: Service animals are allowed on island. All trails on island are wide with low gradation and crushed-gravel substrate. Additionally, there is an accessible 1.5-mile perimeter trail that meets ADA guidelines. Please note that there is limited shade/tree coverage on island.
short_description: Hike one of the drumlins of Spectacle Island to catch beautiful views of the city and harbor.

title: Visit One of the Boston Harbor Islands
accessibility: All piers, docks and gangways are ADA compliant, though gangways may be steep at low tide. Park ferries are generally accessible; contact Boston Harbor Cruises at 617-227-4321 for detailed vessel information. Service animals are allowed on the islands. Spectacle Island Spectacle Island is the only park island that features an accessible 1.5-mile perimeter trail that meets ADA guidelines. All trails on the island are wide with low gradation and crushed-gravel substrate. Visitor Center, exhibits, and multi-stall restrooms are at ground level with no steps. An accessible beach mat and beach wheelchair are available upon request. Georges Island Georges Island features wide paved pathways around the exterior of Fort Warren and throughout island picnic areas. Inside the fort, a mix of paved and stone pathways provide access to much of the structure. The interior of this historic fort includes some narrow passageways, doorway thresholds and steep stone staircases. Visitor Center, exhibits, and multi-stall restrooms are at ground level with no steps, as are single-stall Clivus (composting toilet) units in island picnic areas. Peddocks Island Peddocks Island features wide paved pathways on the East side of the island as well as wooded trails throughout the island. Camping areas are accessed by a mix of paved and dirt paths. Single-stall restrooms and drinking fountains are at ground level with no steps, with additional restrooms down one flight of stairs. Welcome Center and exhibits are several steps up and are accessible by elevator.
short_description: Made up of 34 unique islands and peninsulas, the Boston Harbor Islands have something for everyone. Choose an island and plan your adventure!

title: Hike with a Ranger on Spectacle Island
accessibility: Service animals are allowed on island. All trails on island are wide with low gradation and crushed-gravel substrate. Please note that there is limited shade/tree coverage on island.
short_description: Join a ranger for a hike on Spectacle Island!

title: Fort Tours on Georges Island
accessibility: Service animals are allowed on island. The interior of Fort Warren has several narrow passageways, doorway thresholds, and steep staircases. A mix of stone, and pavement provide access to much of the first level of the fort. Some of the pavement is uneven.
short_description: Join a ranger for a tour of Fort Warren on Georges Island!

title: Take a Lighthouse Cruise
fee_description: Please purchase tickets on the Lighthouse Cruises page on the Boston Harbor Islands partnership website.
accessibility: The Columbia Point is an ADA accessible vessel. There is sometimes a step getting on the vessel, the size of the step varies depending on the tide. Food and water are not available on the boat. Plan to bring your own food and drink. Alcoholic beverages, smoking, and vaping are not permitted on the cruise.
short_description: Cruise Boston’s outer harbor to learn about navigational aids in Boston and the uses of the islands over time.

title: Backcountry Hiking South Bluff
topics: Foothills, Plains and Valleys;Geology;Grasslands;Prairies;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views
accessibility: Hiking South Bluff is off-trail with steep inclines and loose rock.
short_description: Backcountry hiking on South Bluff is difficult and should only be attempted by experienced hikers. Please check in with the ranger at the visitor center.

title: Bicycle Touring

short_description: Bicycling touring in Capitol Reef offers opportunities to explore paved and unpaved roads throughout the park. Explore colorful canyons, beautiful vistas of red rock country, and the verdant Fruita Historic District by bicycle.

title: Lower Cave Tour
fee_description: $20 for adults and $10 for children, Senior and Access Pass holders.
accessibility: There are ladders to enter and exit Lower Cave. Trail is narrow and unpaved.
short_description: In 1924, National Geographic expedition members wrote about the wonders of Lower Cave. Visitors today can see the evidence left behind from those and other explorers.

title: Charlestown Navy Yard: Dive into The History of the Yard at the Visitor Center's Exhibits
topics: Engineering;Industry;Laborer and Worker;Ships and Shipwrecks;US Navy;World War I;World War II
accessibility: The Visitor Center has ramps throughout the space for people with wheelchairs and other mobility devices. Service animals are allowed inside the Charlestown Navy Yard Visitor Center.
short_description: Walk through the exhibits of the Navy Yard's Visitor Center to learn about the history of the Yard and the ingenuity of its workers.

title: Old North Church: Audio Tour
topics: African American Heritage;American Revolution;Architecture and Building;Enslavement;Religion and Spirituality;Churches;American Revolutionary War
fee_description: Some admission packages to Old North Church include the immersive audio guide. Visit Old North Church's Admission and Pricing webpage for up-to-date fees.
accessibility: Old North Church's sanctuary is accessible. Note: To avoid steps in the courtyard while following the Freedom Trail from downtown, you will have to make a left at Unity St., take the right on to Tileston St., then make a right on to Salem St.
short_description: Discover Old North’s secrets and stories with a brand-new audio tour! Available in English or Spanish, the tour weaves together the story of Paul Revere’s famous lantern signal with recent research into the lives of Old North’s free and enslaved Indigenous and Black congregants.

title: Walk the Freedom Trail
topics: African American Heritage;American Revolution;Burial, Cemetery and Gravesite;Colonization and Settlement;Laborer and Worker;Maritime;Maritime - Military;Ships and Shipwrecks;Military;Battlefields;Indigenous and Native Warrior;Infantry and Militia;US Navy;Monuments and Memorials;Religion and Spirituality;Churches;Social Movements;Abolition Movement;Civil Rights;Religious Freedom;Voting Rights and Suffrage;Wars and Conflicts;American Revolutionary War;Civil War;Cold War;Colonial/European Contact Conflicts;French and Indian War;Indian and Frontier Wars;War of 1812;World War I;World War II;Women's History
accessibility: Overall the Freedom Trail follows a route along wide city sidewalks that feature curb cuts. Crosings at stoplights feature both visual and audible crosswalk signals. There are several portions of the trail, however, that traverse stairs. An alternate route is required. The following locations have detours: Stairs to the 54th Massachusetts/Robert Gould Shaw Memorial: When in the Boston Common, head toward the Park Street MBTA station at the intersection of Park and Tremont Streets. Follow the sidewalk up Park Street toward Beacon Street. Stairs to enter the Granary Burying Ground can be bypassed by entering an at-grade entrance off Beacon Street. When at the main entrance at Tremont Street, continue down Tremont to the intersection with Beacon Street. Turn left to head up Beacon Street. The first alleyway to the left ends with an at-grade entrance to the Burying Ground. Old State House can only be entered via stairs. When following the trail from Paul Revere Park to the Old North Church, a detour around the block on Tileston Street is required. Copp's Hill is only accessible by stairs. USS Constitution and USS Cassin Young are historic ships with stairs, ladders, and gangways that move with the tide.
short_description: Originally conceptualized in the 1950s, the Freedom Trail® is an iconic symbol of Boston. Its red brick line snakes through some of the oldest parts of the City, navigating visitors to some of the most significant historic sites in the Downtown, North End, and Charlestown neighborhoods of Boston.

title: Upper Sauma Ridge Trail
accessibility: The trail is steep and very rocky. Footing is uneven and can be slippery.
short_description: Strenuous = 3.2mi/5.15km total; 1,489ft/454m elevation gain; 3-4 hours. Hike a challenging trail through a dense rainforest, surrounded by native trees and birds. Enjoy one of the island’s most beautiful views of Vatia village and Pola Island at the summit.

title: Hike the Callville Summit Trail
fee_description: Callville Summit Trail is in a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: This trail is made up of uneven rocks and gravel as it climbs up to the summit. There is about 150 feet of elevation change throughout the trail up to a high viewpoint overlooking the Boulder Basin of Lake Mead. A hiking pole is recommended.
short_description: From the summit, take in stunning views looking over Callville Bay and beautiful blue Lake Mead.

title: Drive along Northshore Road
topics: Geology;Mountains;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Trails;Roads, Routes and Highways;Wetlands;Wilderness
accessibility: See individual activity/location listings for accessibility information.
short_description: If Lakeshore Road is Lake Mead’s “Main Street”, Northshore Road is its scenic route. Stretching for almost fifty miles, Northshore Road winds its way from modern times next to housing developments through historic geologic periods where the landscape changed from a flat, open plain on the edge of a continent to the rich geologic formations we see today. Northshore Road really is a trip through time.

title: Hike the River Mountains Loop Trail
fee_description: The River Mountains Loop Trail is a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: This trail is 34 miles of a firm paved surface that is easy for bikes and wheelchairs to navigate. Several miles of the trail are level, but there is about 750 feet of elevation change throughout the trail.
short_description: The River Mountains Loop Trail is a non-motorized, paved trail provides visitors with an extensive trail loop offering scenic views, plentiful wildlife, and the vast beauty only the Mojave Desert can offer.

title: Hike the Historic Railroad Trail
fee_description: The Historical Railroad Tunnel Trail is in a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: There is no shade for the first 1.5 miles. The surface is level and made of hardpacked fine gravel that is easy for bikes and wheelchairs to navigate. There are shipping containers in two of the tunnels with short ramps at each end. They protect people from small rocks that infrequently fall from the ceiling.
short_description: The Historic Railroad Trail features incredible vistas of Lake Mead and Boulder Basin and five tunnels – each approximately 25 feet wide.

title: Hike the St. Thomas Trail
fee_description: The Historical Railroad Tunnel Trail is in a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: This trail begins on a slope downhill on loose rocks. The rest of the trail made up of uneven rocks and sand through the foundations of St. Thomas. A hiking pole is recommended.
short_description: Today, remnants of the town are now visible thanks to the lowering water levels of Lake Mead.

title: Stamp Your Passport Book
accessibility: Public areas of the Scotts Bluff National Monument Visitor Center are fully accessbile.
short_description: Stamp your "Passport to Your National Parks" book in the Scotts Bluff National Monument Visitor Center!

title: Become a Scotts Bluff Junior Ranger
accessibility: All public areas of the Scotts Bluff National Monument Visitor Center, where Junior Ranger Activity Books can be picked up and turned in, are fully accessible.
short_description: Earn your Scotts Bluff National Monument Junior Ranger badge!

title: King's Palace Tour
fee_description: $8 for adults and $4 for children, Senior and Access Pass holders. Tour participants must also purchase an entrance fee ticket.
accessibility: The trail is steep in places with steps. Not accessible to wheeled devices.
short_description: The King's Palace Tour takes visitors through four highly decorated chambers and the deepest portion of the cavern open to the public.

title: Hike the Bluffs Trail
fee_description: The Bluffs Trail is in a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: Beginning near campsite #72, this trail is 3.9 miles (6.2 km) on a natural earth surface with uneven rock and gravel. There is about 145 feet of elevation change throughout the trail and some steeper sections to traverse through a wash.
short_description: Bluffs Trail overlooks the Las Vegas Bay and Las Vegas Wash, where visitors can see a stark contrast in vegetation between wet and dry areas.

title: Hike the Wetlands Trail
fee_description: The Wetlands Trail is in a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: This trail is an unmaintained route. It is 1.5 miles on a natural earth surface with uneven rocks, gravel, and sand. There is about 110 feet of elevation change throughout the trail, with the steepest part made into large steps with some logs to support the rocks and gravel. A hiking pole is recommended.
short_description: The Wetlands Trail follows a dry dirt trail down to the flowing Las Vegas Wash, where water from the Las Vegas Valley dispenses into Lake Mead and shapes the landscape through erosion.

title: Hike the Northshore Summit Trail
fee_description: The Northshore Trail is in a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: This trail is an unmaintained route. It is 1.0 miles (1.6 km) on a natural earth surface with some uneven rocks and gravel. With about 200 feet of elevation change, this trail climbs up to a hilltop to a panoramic view of the surrounding area.
short_description: A perfect place to take in the desert in all its vastness and striking colors.

title: Hike the Redstone Trail
fee_description: Redstone Trail is a fee area, like the rest of the park. Keep your park pass or proof of admission with your vehicle for rangers to inspect.
accessibility: The trailhead begins next to the paved sidewalk around the picnic tables and restrooms. This trail is an unmaintained route. The majority of the trail is on loose sand and gravel with about 80 feet of elevation change.
short_description: The fiery eroded formations on this trail were once part of a vast desert landscape.

title: Take a Pullman Ranger-Guided Tour
topics: African American Heritage;Architecture and Building;Commerce;Engineering;Immigration;Industry;Factories;Laborer and Worker;Labor Movement;Trains and Railroads;Urban America
accessibility: Ranger tours are wheelchair accessible and follow urban sidewalks and streets. ASL interpreters are available with advanced notice for ranger led tours. Please email PULL_visitorinfo@nps.gov or call (773) 928-7257 for accommodations.
short_description: Park Ranger Tours

title: Boating in Canyonlands
accessibility: Flows in Canyonlands range from flatwater perfect for canoes, sea kayaks and other shallow-water boats, to challenging stretches of Class III to V whitewater and are often constantly changing. Watercrafts designed with accessibilty in mind are highly recommended to navigate all waterways in Canyonlands.
short_description: The Colorado and Green rivers have played a significant role in shaping the landscape of Canyonlands. Boating is a great way to see the park from the bottom up, and affords boaters a unique perspective.

title: Watch the Sunset
duration: Depending on the trail you choose, allow yourself half an hour to four hours.
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: Trails vary from short, easy walks (less than a mile roundtrip), to moderate and strenuous trails with over 400 feet of elevation change. Trail surfaces include slickrock, packed dirt, stone steps, and loose gravel. None of these trails are paved.
short_description: Watch the sunset from various scenic points in Capitol Reef. Take an easy stroll or a strenuous hike as the sun goes down. Don't forget to bring a headlamp.

title: Visit the Petroglyph Panel
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: Two wooden boardwalks provide access to view the petroglyphs. Two free stationary binoculars are available to get a closer look at them.
short_description: From 600 to 1300 C.E., native people of the Fremont Culture made their home at Capitol Reef. Petroglyphs carved into the Wingate sandstone remind us of their time.

title: Scenic Drive Tour
topics: Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Roads, Routes and Highways
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: The Scenic Drive is a paved road, with beautiful vistas of red, orange, and white cliffs, as well as deep narrow canyons.
short_description: Take Capitol Reef's Scenic Drive, and experience colorful cliffs and deep narrow canyons from the comfort of your vehicle.

title: Hike in the South (Waterpocket) District
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: Trail surfaces include slickrock, packed dirt, sand, and rocky washes. None of these trails are paved. Service animals are allowed.
short_description: Get to know the South (Waterpocket) District on foot by hiking an easy trail or strenuous backcountry route. Many of these hikes are accessible only by unpaved roads.

title: Picnic
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: In the Doc Insglesby Picnic Area, a paved trail leads to restrooms with running water (open seasonally). A sloped, grassy lawn has places for picnic blankets and some tables, including those with accessible seating. In Capitol Gorge, a few tables are wheelchair accessible, but there is not a ramp to access the tables from the parking lot.
short_description: Enjoy a picnic in Capitol Reef National Park! In the Fruita Historic District, look for the Doc Inglesby and Chesnut picnic areas, as well as tables and a water fountain near the Gifford House. At the end of Capitol Gorge Road, off the Scenic Drive, there are covered picnic tables as well as a pit toilet.

title: Hike Cathedral Valley
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: Trail surfaces include slickrock, packed dirt, stone steps, and loose gravel. None of these trails are paved. Service animals are allowed.
short_description: Explore Cathedral Valley by foot. These hikes are accessible only by rough unpaved roads. A high clearance vehicle is necessary and four-wheel drive is recommended at times.

title: Hike an Easy or Moderate Trail
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: Trails vary from short, easy walks (less than a mile roundtrip), to moderate trails with over 400 feet of elevation change. Trail surfaces include slickrock, packed dirt, stone steps, and loose gravel. None of these trails are paved. Service animals are allowed.
short_description: Hike an easy or moderate trail to see panoramic views or to experience a deep sandstone canyon.

title: Driving the Burr Trail
topics: Canyons and Canyonlands;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Roads, Routes and Highways;Wilderness
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: Although in dry weather the Burr Trail is easily accessible to passenger cars, wet weather may make the road impassable even for 4-wheel drive vehicles. Check with rangers or local officials for weather and road conditions. Recreational Vehicles and trailers are not recommended.
short_description: Drive the scenic Burr Trail from Glen Canyon's Bullfrog district, along the bottom of Capitol Reef, through Grand Staircase, to Boulder, UT. Distance: 67 miles (108 km) one-way Mix of paved and dirt roads, impassable when wet Four-wheel drive sometimes required. No RVs.

title: Hike a Strenuous Trail
fee_description: A fee is required for recreating within Capitol Reef National Park.
accessibility: Trail surfaces include slickrock, packed dirt, stone steps, and loose gravel. None of these trails are paved. Service animals are allowed.
short_description: Hike a strenuous trail to view dramatic geologic formations and spectacular vistas.

title: Stargazing at Joshua Tree
accessibility: The terrain of the stargazing areas may be suitable for some wheelchairs, but not all. Service animals are allowed. Emotional support animals are allowed on-leash within 100 feet of the parking lot, but are not allowed on trails.
short_description: Enjoy Joshua Tree National Park's amazing night sky.

title: Winter Fun at Saratoga
accessibility: The Wilkinson Trail is NOT accessible. Visitor Center From the start of December to the end of February, the Visitor Center is generally open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm. Check our operating hours for updates and our alerts for closures. Parking Two spaces available in main parking lot at bottom of ramp. Ramp has a steep incline to visitor center; additional parking is available on Roosevelt Rd. Entrance Automatic front doors (2 sets) open outwards, ramp and automatic rear door opens outwards Restrooms Partially accessible indoor restrooms are available in the visitor center - a handicap stall is available, but there is no automatic door. A partially accessible outdoor portable toilet is available in the lower level of the visitor center parking area near the tour road entrance. Water A water bottle fill station is located inside visitor center between restrooms. A water fountain is located outside off ramp from main parking lot. The water from the fountain contains sodium in excess of 20 mg/L. Picnic tables Handicap accessible picnic area is accessible from main parking lot, picnic tables are also available behind visitor center Restrooms Partially accessible outdoor portable toilets are available at tour road entrance and a composting toilet is available at tour road stop 7. Walkways All tour road stops have paved walkways that meet ADA grade and slope requirements. Driving Tour Road (Dec.-Apr.) The tour road is closed to vehicles. NPS staff will plow the tour road for pedestrian use from the parking lot to the "access road," which is a distance of about 1/2 mile; and from the end of the "access" to "Stop 8," which is a distance of about 2 miles. While the road is plowed, slippery or wintry conditions may still exist and visitors should exercise extreme caution.
short_description: Learn about fun winter activities as Saratoga National Historical Park!

title: Visit Glen Haven Historic Village
topics: Logging and Timber Cutting;Mills;Maritime;Ships and Shipwrecks;US Coast Guard
fee_description: Aside from a park pass, there is no separate fee for visiting Glen Haven. Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore charges a variety of fees, depending on how a visitor arrives at the park, and whether they're part of a commercial tour group or not. Visit the fees page to find the pass that is best for you.
accessibility: Physical and Mobility Needs Sand Wheelchairs are available at the Maritime Museum boathouse and at the Cannery to enable disabled individuals to enjoy the dunes and beaches. You must present a driver's license or similar identification. The chairs are available on a first-come, first-served basis; we don't take reservations. The Blacksmith Shop in Glen Haven Historic Village is a fully functioning shop and is accessible by a ramp built up to the front double doors. There is ample space inside the shop to see exhibits and watch the blacksmith and carpentry demonstrations from a safe distance. Benches are provided. D.H. Day General Store in Glen Haven is accessible. Parking is provided in the front with a ramped concrete path to the entrance. The interior space includes both displays and reproduction sales items from the late 1920s and early 1930s for purchase. The first floor of the Ranger Station is also fully accessible and is in the same structure as the D.H. Day Store. Restrooms in Glen Haven are ramped and accessible with running water and a diaper changing station. Beach dressing areas are included. The Cannery Boat Museum is accessible. The adjoining picnic area has picnic tables and raised grills. While the parking area is sandy, it is next to the beach and provides a beautiful view of Sleeping Bear Bay and the Manitou Islands. There is a hard surfaced beach deck with benches. A sand wheelchair is available for use at the site. Coast Guard Station Life-Saving Museum has accessible parking with hardened surfaces leading to the Boathouse exhibit. This is accessible by wheelchair, and a boardwalk leads from there to the beach. The entrance to the Station House requires stair climbing and is not wheelchair accessible. Benches facing the lake are located on the porch for those who can climb the stairs. A sand wheelchair is available for use at the site. Park Brochure The park brochure is available in both braille and audio described/text only versions. The braille park brochure is available as a downloadable file for home printing on braille-compatible equipment. You may also request a braille copy to be sent to you by mail. Braille brochures are not typically available on-hand in the visitor center. The Park Brochure Formats page contains information on accessing the brochure in alternative formats. This page also includes a full text-only version of the brochure, compatible with most screen readers. Service Animals Service animals are allowed in Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore. If needed, read a definition of service animal . An emotional support animal is not a qualified service animal. For information on animals that do not qualify as service animals, please see our information on pets in the park . Anywhere that you wish to go in Sleeping Bear Dunes, your service animal may go, too. There are some unique aspects of visiting our wilderness areas to keep in mind, however.
short_description: Glen Haven is the best-preserved cord wood station on the eastern shore of Lake Michigan, and perhaps in the entire Great Lakes. It was a company town, eventually diversifying into farming, canning of fruit, and tourism. Today, the history of Glen Haven is still preserved within several buildings that you can visit during your trip to Sleeping Bear Dunes. In the summer, these buildings are open to visit and staffed with knowledgeable and friendly volunteers.

title: Explore Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive
fee_description: Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore charges a variety of fees, depending on how a visitor arrives at the park, and whether they're part of a commercial tour group or not. Visit the fees page to find the pass that is best for you.
accessibility: Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive offers a 7.4 mile loop with beautiful views of Lake Michigan, the Glen Lakes, and the dunes, much of which can be appreciated through the vehicle windows. The twelve stops along the way allow for a leisurely pace. Accessible parking and toilets are at four locations: the entrance trailer parking area, Picnic Mountain, #9 Lake Michigan Overlook, and #11 North Bar Lake Overlook and picnic area. Running water and flush toilets are accessible at Picnic Mountain. A hard-surfaced picnic area with table and raised grill is also available. The #3 Dunes Overlook has a ramped deck with two levels lined with benches. The stunning panorama of dunes and lake views may also be seen from the circle drive. The #9 Lake Michigan Overlook and #10 Sleeping Bear Dune Overlook are not handicap accessible and require following a steep asphalt trail and loose sand. The #11 North Bar Lake Overlook picnic area is fairly flat with tables and raised grills located near accessible parking. Accessible vault toilets are provided, but there is no running water at this location.
short_description: Enjoy spectacular views of Glen Lake, undulating sand dunes, and breathtaking views of the grandest of all dunes, with shimmering Lake Michigan as the backdrop. Wind through cool forests of sugar maple and beech trees. Take a moment along the way to enjoy a picnic, take a walk, or just linger in the sunshine.

title: Get a Passport Stamp at Kenai Fjords National Park
accessibility: The Kenai Fjords National Park Visitor Center and Exit Glacier Nature Centers are fully accessible. Service animals are allowed.
short_description: Get your Kenai Fjords National Park cancellation stamps and more.

title: Visit the Cabrillo Tidepools
topics: Animals;Coasts, Islands and Atolls;Geology;Oceans;Scenic Views;Unique Species
accessibility: Navigating the terrain at the tidepools requires navigating over slippery and uneven surfaces. To reach the tidepools you must travel 1/4 to 1/2 miles down a dirt path with approximately 100 feet of elevation change.
short_description: Learn about visiting the tidepools at Cabrillo National Monument!

title: Hike Little River Trail
fee_description: Parking tags are required for all vehicles parking for longer than 15 minutes.
accessibility: This trail is not ADA accessible. For the first 2.7 miles, the trail is relatively wide and flat, featuring a mix of crushed stone and occasional roots and rocks. While a few sections are slightly steeper, the overall path is considered leisurely, making it ideal for a relaxed hike. Around mile marker 2.5, the trail begins to narrow and transitions from a roadbed to a more natural path. After passing the junction with Rough Creek Trail at approximately 4.5 miles, the terrain becomes rockier and more challenging. The final stretch includes three water crossings, which require careful footing. A section of this trail has been assessed using the High-Efficiency Trail Assessment Process (HETAP) to provide objective information such as grade and slope. HETAP data collected on the first 0.9 miles of this trail: The typical slope is 3.2%. The typical cross slope/grade in the trail side-to-side , is 2.0%, with a maximum of 19.1%. The typical width is 10.6 feet (3.22 meters) with a minimum of 3.3 feet (1.02 meters). The trail surface is composed of aggregate material and gravel. GRIT Freedom Chairs are available for free checkout on a first-come, first-serve basis for the first 2.7 miles (one-way) of this trail to the junction with Huskey Gap Trail. Use descriptions, maps, and photos to determine which hikes are suitable for you. For information about the reservation process and other trail segments where GRIT Freedom Chairs can be used, visit the trail accessibility page.
short_description: Once a railroad bed, the Little River Trail now offers a peaceful hike through the Elkmont area of Great Smoky Mountains National Park. As you follow the river’s gentle flow, you’ll pass remnants of the old Elkmont community—stone chimneys and foundations quietly tucked into the forest.

title: Swimming in Lake Powell
fee_description: Standard entrance fees and vessel fees apply for Glen Canyon National Recreation Area. There are no additional fees for swimming.
accessibility: Swimming in Lake Powell is an activity that could be enjoyed by people at any level of mobility, sightedness, hearing, or sensory issues. If you are an adult who can swim, you can swim in Lake Powell. If you are at all hesitant about your swimming capabilities, or just if you want to float, we highly recommend wearing a lifejacket that fits while in the water. Children under 12 years old, regardless of ability, must wear a lifejacket while in the water. There are few access points to the water if you do not have a boat. Of the five swimming areas listed, only Wahweap Swim Beach has a trail that would be usable by a wheelchair equipped with sand/beach wheels. All of the other spots are too sandy or rocky for wheelchair access. Service animals are welcome to enjoy the water, as are pets, so keep an eye on your helper around errant pets.
short_description: Swimming is a popular activity at Lake Powell, especially in the summer when water temperatures can surpass 80 degrees Fahrenheit. Please be aware that there are no life guards or officially designated swim beaches at Lake Powell or on the Colorado River. Water Quality conditions can change at your favorite swim areas.

title: Hike Cholla Cactus Garden
accessibility: This is a dirt trail that is mostly flat with occasional mild inclines. Pets are not allowed on this trail, but service animals are welcome. Service animals must remain on a 6-foot (1.8 meter) leash at all times.
short_description: An easy quarter mile hike through a cholla patch along Pinto Basin Road.

title: Hike Skull Rock
accessibility: The Skull Rock Trail contains various terrain types, including deep sand, hard pack dirt, and uneven rocky surfaces. The trail is relatively flat and has a 150 feet total elevation change. The trail widens to a 6+ feet across in some areas but is as narrow as 2 feet in certain areas. A section of the trail near the Jumbo Rocks Campground has rocky steps that ascend about 20-40 feet of elevation. The trail is not accessible for people using wheelchairs. Some wheelchair users are comfortable on the section of the trail that merges with the Jumbo Rock campground road. However, this road is uneven and often covered in rocks and sand and is not accessible for every type of wheelchair. Pets and emotional support animals are not allowed on trails, but service animals are welcome. Service animals must remain on a 6-foot (1.8 meter) leash at all times.
short_description: A relatively flat, 1.7-mile loop trail. Hike through the large, granite boulder fields around the Jumbo Rocks area, including one near Park Boulevard that closely resembles a Skull.

title: Park Passport Stamps at Fort Smith NHS

accessibility: The passport stamps are located in the visitor center lobby. Entrance is step-free with button-operated automatic doors. Service animals are allowed.
short_description: Stamp your passport! Stamps are available inside the visitor center lobby at Fort Smith National Historic Site.

accessibility: There are no trails or facilities in Kobuk Valley National Park.
short_description: Want a nice mild float on a wild river? The Kobuk River may be a great option for wilderness adventure and zen-like floating in Kobuk Valley National Park.

title: Exhibit - First Things First: FDR, Disability, & Access
accessibility: Automatic door entrance over 32 inches in width. Manuevering clearance throughout exhibit gallery. ADA compliant reader rail height for seated individuals. High color contrast and large, sans serif text in dyslexia-friendly layouts on each graphic panel. Approachable images on reader rails. Tactile gallery map. Tactile scaled bronze model of FDR's wheelchair. Audio description of exhibit content available on the NPS app in July 2025.
short_description: In 1921, FDR became paralyzed at the age of 39. Before he could return to politics, he first had to figure out how to get around. Inaccessible places create barriers that effectively disable us from full and equal participation in society. FDR used wheelchairs, crutches, canes, leg braces, handrails, automobiles, ramps, and other objects to navigate the social and physical barriers people with disabilities face every day.

title: Enjoy the Night Sky
accessibility: The path to the Cedar Pass Amphitheater from the parking lot is an accessible paved ramp. Service animals are allowed at the Amphitheater.
short_description: Night Sky Viewings are a great way to see the dark skies of the Badlands. Park rangers and astronomy volunteers are available to point out objects in the night sky and help you look through telescopes.

title: Moose-Wilson Road in Winter
fee_description: A general fee is charged to enter Grand Teton National Park.
accessibility: During winter the Moose-Wilson Road is closed from the south at the Granite Trailhead and from the north at the Death Canyon Junction, providing 3 miles (4.8 km) of walking, skiing, and snowshoeing. As you ski or snowshoe on the road you will wind through forest and marsh habitats, covered in deep snow and ice. Be aware that not all is frozen underfoot, thin ice can be dangerous—use caution. Jackson Hole area organizations provide accessible equipment and lessons so people of all abilities can explore the park in winter, call 307-739-3399 for more information. Qualified service animals trained to assist people with disabilities are allowed in throughout the park and in all park facilities. Your service animal may accompany you anywhere. We request that you fill out a Service Animal acknowledgement form at one of the visitor centers when you arrive. More information see the parks service animal information.
short_description: The Moose-Wilson Road is a corridor road connecting the towns of Moose and Wilson. In the winter the road is closed from the south at the Granite Trailhead and from the north at the Death Canyon Junction, providing 3 miles (4.8 km) of walking, skiing, and snowshoeing. As you ski or snowshoe on the road you will wind through forest and marsh habitats, covered in deep snow and ice. Be aware that not all is frozen underfoot, thin ice can be dangerous—use caution.

title: Teton Park Road in Winter
fee_description: A general fee is charged to enter Grand Teton National Park.
