short_description: Enjoy Lassen’s winter wonderland by snowshoe! Meander along the park highway route (snow-covered Hwy 89), circuit an icy lake, visit boiling hydrothermal features, or, for intrepid explorers, summit a snowy peak.

title: Hike Fortynine Palms Oasis
accessibility: This trail is a mix of dirt, sand, and rock. This trail climbs over steep ridges with steps in both directions Pets are not allowed on this trail, but service animals are welcome. Service animals must remain on a 6-foot (1.8 meter) leash at all times.
short_description: A difficult three mile hike to a desert oasis.

title: Become a Junior Ranger at Sitka National Historical Park
topics: Arts;Colonization and Settlement;Rainforest;Native American Heritage;River and Riparian;Trails
accessibility: The Jr. Ranger program is a booklet that features a variety of activities for children.
short_description: Become a Junior Ranger! Learn about Tlingit culture, the rainforest, Russian American history, and the coastal environment. You'll earn an official badge so that you will not forget how important you are to the National Park Service.

title: Picnicking at Nicodemus
accessibility: Picnic tables, sun shelters, and outdoor porta-potties are wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Picnic areas are available at Nicodemus with picnic tables, sun shelters, grills, and water.

title: Photography and Art
accessibility: Photography at Nicodemus NHS is accessible to all visitors by car, wheelchair, or on foot.
short_description: Taking photos in Kansas? What's even out there? Nicodemus has plenty of landscapes, buildings, wildlife, and skies that you will want to capture with photos.

title: Keweenaw NHP Ranger Programs
topics: Ruins;Architecture and Building;Photography;Engineering;Geology;Mineral Deposits;Immigration;Mining;Laborer and Worker;Labor Movement
fee_description: Ranger Programs are free.
accessibility: Downtown Calumet walks are accessible with assistance. Quincy Mine Ruins Hikes are not accessible as they cover uneven terrain.
short_description: Experience Keweenaw NHP with a ranger guided walk!

title: Bonita Creek Loop
accessibility: This is an easy 0.2 mile trail that is wheelchair accessible. There is no elevation change and pets are allowed on the trail.
short_description: This Bonita Creek loops around the picnic area and takes you along the intermittent Bonita Creek. Watch for Apache plume and prickly poppy flowers in spring and early summer. Arizona whitetail deer are frequently seen in the lower portion of Bonita Canyon. This is a good trail to view grassland birds.

title: Hike The Mount Finlayson Loop Trail
accessibility: This is a moderate trail that is 2.9 miles long and includes 380 feet of elevation gain.
short_description: This popular trail is a 2.9 mile loop. It visits numerous ecosystems and provides excellent views of the Cascades and Olympic Mountains.

title: Visit Craters in Winter
fee_description: Snowshoes may be borrowed from the visitor center when open for a suggested donation of $5 per pair. There is no entrance fee when the Loop Road is closed to vehicles.
accessibility: During winter, Craters of the Moon is covered in snow. The park road, typically used to access the park's trails and natural features, is closed to motorized travel. Snow clearing does not take place along the Loop Road or on any trails in the winter. Travel through the park is via ski or snowshoe. The groomed ski track is mostly easy to moderate with one steep 10% grade near Inferno Cone. The marked Snowshoe Trail is moderately strenuous with several steep inclines. Pits and jagged rocks may be encountered off-trail. Roads, walkways, and parking areas may be covered in slippery ice or snow. Hiking trails are completely covered by snow in winter and may have patches of ice or snow from early fall into late spring.
short_description: Tour a lava wonderland blanketed in snow. Winter visitors can enjoy skiing the groomed park road or venture into the park on snowshoes.

title: Hike Goldmine Loop via Tunnel Bypass Trail
fee_description: A parking tag is required to park in the Smokies for more than 15 minutes.
accessibility: Some rocky areas and shallow stream crossings.
short_description: Hike 4 miles (6.4 km) on Lakeshore and Goldmine Loop trails through a hardwood forest filled with signs of old homesites and farms. This trail is moderate but includes some rocky areas and shallow stream crossings.

title: Friendship Hill Junior Ranger
topics: Animals;Ruins;Architecture and Building;Forests and Woodlands;Industry;Logging and Timber Cutting;Landscape Design;Conservation Movement;Transportation;Roads, Routes and Highways
fee_description: The Junior Ranger Adventure Book is free. Participants will be offered a choice between a Friendship Hill Junior Ranger Badge or Embroidered Patch at no charge.
accessibility: The places Friendship Hill Junior Rangers are required to visit are accessible via paved path. An elevator is available in the Gallatin House to access the second floor. The second floor Stone House bedrooms are not available via wheelchairs or strollers.
short_description: The Friendship Hill Junior Ranger program is completed on-site and includes different levels of activities for children age 6-12

title: Friendship Hill Senior Ranger
topics: Animals;Architecture and Building;Forests and Woodlands;Industry;Landscape Design;Science, Technology and Innovation;Conservation Movement;Trails;Transportation;Roads, Routes and Highways;Wars and Conflicts;Mexican War;War of 1812
fee_description: The Senior Ranger Activity Book is provided free. Participants will be offered a choice between a Friendship Hill Senior Ranger Badge or Embroidered Patch at no charge.
accessibility: The places Friendship Hill Senior Rangers are required to visit are accessible via paved path. An elevator is available in the Gallatin House to access the second floor. The second floor Stone House bedrooms are not available via wheelchairs or strollers.
short_description: The Friendship Hill Senior Ranger Program is completed on-site and includes different levels of activities for visitors ages 13 and up, including adults!

title: Become a Junior Ranger at Boston African American National Historic Site
accessibility: To download an accessible version of the Junior Ranger book, visit the Park's Junior Ranger page.
short_description: Become a Junior Ranger at Boston African American National Historic Site by learning about the sites along the Black Heritage Trail Trail® here in Boston.

title: Paul Revere House: Step Back in Time at The Revere's Family Home
fee_description: For updated information on prices, please visit their "Hours & Prices" page.
accessibility: The Paul Revere House is fully accessible for individuals who use wheelchairs or are mobility impaired. The house is accessible on the first floor via the courtyard ramps. The second floor is accessed by taking the elevator in the visitor center and then connecting to the house via the walkway. There are also materials for visually impaired and deaf/hard of hearing individuals. Service animals are welcome. Please check The Paul Revere House's Accessibility page for more information.
short_description: Take a self-guided tour through the well-preserved rooms where Paul Revere and his family lived for about twenty years.

title: Become a Junior Ranger at Boston National Historical Park
accessibility: The Junior Ranger book is accessible. For more accessibility information about the park and partner sites, please visit their websites.
short_description: Become a Junior Ranger at Boston National Historical Park by learning about the sites along the Freedom Trail® here in Boston.

title: Bunker Hill: Uncover the Stories Behind the Battle and Monument at the Museum
topics: American Revolution;Military;Infantry and Militia;American Revolutionary War
accessibility: The Bunker Hill Museum has an elevator to take visitors to exhibit floors. Service animals are allowed inside the Bunker Hill Museum.
short_description: At the exhibits of the Bunker Hill Museum, visitors can explore more about the Battle of Bunker Hill, the construction of the Bunker Hill Monument, the memory of the battle, and the history of the Charlestown neighborhood.

title: Watch the Charlestown Navy Yard Orientation Film
topics: Laborer and Worker;Ships and Shipwrecks;US Navy;World War I;World War II
accessibility: The Visitor Center Theater is accessible via ramp. There are captions for the film. Service animals are allowed inside the Charlestown Navy Yard Visitor Center.
short_description: Before exploring the Charlestown Navy Yard, take a few minutes to watch an introductory film on the Charlestown Navy Yard.

title: Fishing in the Everglades
fee_description: A Florida freshwater fishing license is required to fish in freshwater or to possess fresh water species. A Florida saltwater fishing license is required to fish in saltwater or to possess saltwater species. Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information .
accessibility: Most lake and shoreline areas in Everglades National Park are rocky and are not free from rough terrain. Accessible dock and pier fishing in the Flamingo Marina is not allowed during daylight hours.
short_description: One third of Everglades National Park is covered by water, creating excellent boating and fishing opportunities! Snapper, sea trout, redfish, bass, and bluegill are plentiful. Saltwater fishing includes Florida Bay, the Ten Thousand Islands, and elsewhere in the park's coastal zone.

title: Hike to Young Hill
accessibility: This is a moderate hike along an unpaved trail. It is 1.9 miles round trip and includes 566 feet of elevation gain.
short_description: The hike to the top of Young Hill provides a panoramic view of San Juan Island’s bays, English Camp, and Vancouver Island.

title: Hike the Mitchell Hill Moderate Loop
accessibility: This is a moderate hike on an uneven, unpaved trail. It is 2.5 miles round trip and inclueds 438 feet of elevation gain.
short_description: The Mitchell Hill Moderate Loop incorporates some of the best trail segments along a slightly more challenging route. The trail takes you through a dense cedar grove and to the top of Mitchell Hill.

title: Hike the Mitchell Hill Easy Loop
accessibility: This is an easy 1.6 mile round-trip trail along a level, unpaved path. There is approximately 155 feet of elevation gain.
short_description: The Mitchell Hill Easy Loop follows the Inner Loop Road trail - a picturesque journey through the lush landscapes at English Camp.

title: Enjoy a Winter Wonderland at Paradise
topics: Animals;Architecture and Building;Explorers and Expeditions;Geology;Glaciers;Mountains;Native American Heritage;Night Sky;Scenic Views;Trails;Volcanoes;Waterfalls;Watersheds
fee_description: Park entrance fee required. No fees for any activities. Permits are required for winter camping.
accessibility: In winter, paths can be snow covered and often icy. Paradise is open as winter road conditions allow. The Jackson Visitor Center is accessible to wheelchairs. The exhibits, theater, dining area, restrooms and general services are accessible. The Jackson Visitor Center exhibits can be explored with an audio description tour. Listening devices for the tour can be checked out at the front desk. The park film and exhibit videos in the vistor center are captioned. Assistive listening devices for the film can be checked out at the front desk. See accessibility page for more details.
short_description: Winter brings into focus a frosty view of the mountain. An abundance of snow creates a winter recreation paradise, but also brings the challenges of icy, snowy roads. The road to Paradise is plowed, when possible, to allow access. Spend hours at Paradise or add a stop in Longmire to make a full day of winter fun.

title: Hike Uplands Trail - South Rim
accessibility: This unpaved, narrow trail is not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: This .9-mile (1.4 km) trail links the Rim Rock Trail (near the campground) to the upper Oak Flat Loop Trail near the South Rim Visitor Center.

title: Hike the Bell Point Loop
accessibility: 1.2 miles round trip 40 ft elevation gain
short_description: The Bell Point trail traverses a mature madrona forest and hugs the shores of Garrison Bay and Westcott Bay.

title: Become a Fort Pulaski Jr. Ranger
accessibility: The Fort Pulaski Junior Ranger Book is accessible for everyone of all ages. The activities can be done without visiting the fort, if needed. We do not have a braille version of the book.
short_description: Explore, Learn, and Protect by becoming a Junior Ranger.

title: Explore Fort Pulaski
topics: African American Heritage;Architecture and Building;Engineering;Forts;Military;US Army;Civil War
fee_description: Entrance fees apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: Fort Pulaski is accessible via a paved walkway from the parking lot and visitor center. Exhibit rooms and casemates have accessible ramps for entrance. The terreplein (top floor) is only reachable by steep staircases. Please visit the Accessibility page for specific information about accessibility in the park.
short_description: Step back in time by exploring the historic Fort Pulaski, the best-preserved fort of its kind.

title: Explore the Cavern at Your Own Pace
fee_description: Adults (ages 16 and older): $15 per person Children (ages 15 and under): Free If you are entering with a pass, please visit the ticket counter for your free admission ticket.
accessibility: A portion of the Big Room Trail is wheelchair accessible. More information is available in the Accessibility brochure. The Natural Entrance Trail is a steep grade and is not accessible for safety.
short_description: The Big Room and Natural Entrance trails can be enjoyed at your own pace. The Big Room Trail is easy to moderate in difficulty. The Natural Entrance Trail is strenuous. Enjoy one or both to experience a variety of cave formations.

title: Hike to Grandma's Cove
accessibility: The hike to Grandma's cove is a 1 mile round trip hike along an unpaved trail. The trail descends 150 feet to the cove. The decent to the cove is steep and may be difficult for some hikers.
short_description: The hike to Grandma's Cove is one mile round trip and visits a sheltered ocean cove great for swimming and looking at tide pools.

title: Hike to Fourth of July Beach
accessibility: This is a 200 ft, unpaved trail from the parking lot to the beach. The path may be uneven and requires stepping down to the beach.
short_description: This beach access is a great way to explore the shoreline and the lagoons. Walking south will take you to Old Town Lagoon.

title: Hike the South Beach Trail
accessibility: The beaches of San Juan Island all take a walk of 100 feet or more to reach. Many of these areas are uneven and narrow trails that may traverse sand without stabilizing features. All pocket beaches descend down fairly steep trails. Unfortunately, no trails at American Camp meet all ADA standards for trails. However, there are some trails that most visitors with mobility impairment find very easy to navigate! This includes the trail from the visitor center to The Redoubt, and some of the trails that start at the Jakle's Lagoon parking lot. Please contact the American Camp visitor center for specific information.
short_description: Visit South Beach via this short 1 mile hike! The trail travels through the American Camp prairie; keep an eye out for foxes, bald eagles, and rabbits.

title: Hike the Jakle's Lagoon Nature Trail
accessibility: This is an easy trail along an unpaved trail. It is a 1 mile long loop with 70 feet of elevation gain.
short_description: This 1 mile trail is an excellent place to take young people to learn more about our environment. Informational waysides along the trail describe the diverse forest ecosystem here.

title: Hike the Old Military Road Trail
accessibility: The trail is 0.6 miles in the American Camp section, however the trail continues longer outside of the park. It is an unpaved trail that crosses Cattle Point Road and includes 88 feet of elevation gain.
short_description: The Old Military Road Trail (also known and more often signed as “The American Camp Trail”) is a 1 mile trail that takes visitors from the American Camp Visitor Center to the Frazer Homestead Preserve.

title: American Camp History Walk
accessibility: This is an easy 1 mile hike along an level, unpaved trail.
short_description: Embark on a captivating 1 mile guided walk through San Juan Island National Historical Park, where you can relive the intriguing events of the Pig War. Interpretive waysides provide historical insight into the life of soldiers at American Camp.

title: Hike the Bluff Trail
accessibility: This is an easy unpaved trail that is 0.8 miles one way. It includes 53 feet of elevation gain.
short_description: The Bluff Trail is a phenomenal way to experience the environmental richness of American Camp. Keep an eye out for orca whales in the Salish Sea.

title: Hike Officer's Hill
accessibility: This is a short 0.3 mile hike along an unpaved trail that includes 127 feet of elevation gain. There are stairs leading to the formal garden.
short_description: The trails surrounding the Officers’ Quarters at English Camp offer a captivating journey through history and nature.

title: Hike the Westcott Bay Trail
accessibility: This trail is 0.6 miles one way from Bell Point Trail to Westcott Bay. Is is unpaved and includes 80 feet of elevation gain.
short_description: The Westcott Bay Trail is a 1.0 mile trail that hugs the shore of Westcott Bay, a tranquil section of shoreline to the East of English Camp.

title: Cross-Country Skiing in Rocky Mountain National Park
fee_description: Park entrance fees are requied to enter the park. There are no additional fees for Cross-Country Skiing.
accessibility: There are no groomed trails for Cross-Country Skiing inside the park. Visitors often create and maintain ski trails at popular trailheads.
short_description: Cross-country skiing can be an enjoyable way to experience the winter season at Rocky. There is typically enough snow for skiing beginning in December through late March. Visit the west side of the park and enjoy a variety of cross-country skiing terrain.

title: Visit Fort Pulaski's Visitor Center
fee_description: Entry to the Visitor Center is included in the park's entrance fees.
accessibility: The Visitor Center has an entrance ramp and automatic doors. Interior doors (to the theater) are not automatic and swing outward. Closed captioning is availble on both video presentations.
short_description: The best place to start your visit to Fort Pulaski!

title: Watch Fort Pulaski's Park Film
fee_description: Entry to the Visitor Center is included in the park's entrance fees.
accessibility: The Visitor Center has an entrance ramp and automatic doors. Interior doors (to the theater) are not automatic and swing outward. Closed captioning is availble on video presentations.
short_description: Twenty-minute film that explores the history of Fort Pulaski from its construction through the end of the 20th century.

title: Clover Creek Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: There are accessible parking spots at the Wuksachi Village parking area. When Wuksachi Lodge is open, there are accessible flush toilets and drinking fountains available.
short_description: This one-way trail is currently marked to the Twin Lakes hiking trail junction. Return to Wuksachi on the same trail.

title: Panther Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: There are accessible parking spots and accessible flush toilets available at the Wolverton parking lot.
short_description: Taking its name from Panther Gap (8,600 feet), the Panther Trail is part of a difficult loop for experienced skiers. Steep grades and dense forests guard the great views from Panther Gap.

title: Trail of the Sequoias Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: General parking is available across the street from the Giant Forest Museum. Accessible parking is available next to the Giant Forest Museum and at the Big Trees Trailhead. Accessible restrooms are available at the Giant Forest Museum.
short_description: A challenging alternative to the Crescent Trail, the Trail of the Sequoias explores the eastern edge of the Giant Forest. This trail is not for novice skiers.

title: Crescent Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: There are accessible parking spots and accessible restrooms available at the Accessible Sherman Tree Parking lot. Parking is limited in winter.
short_description: The trail connects the General Sherman Tree with the end of Crescent Meadow Road (see Crescent Meadow Road Trail). The trail passes through the heart of the Giant Forest. The skiing is mostly easy, but has several short grades that require turning through the thick forest.

title: Old Lodgepole Road Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: Accessible parking is available at the Lodgepole Visitor Center and at the base of the trailhead. Restrooms are not available.
short_description: This old road connects the Lodgepole Visitor Center with the General Sherman Tree. The skiing is easy, except for a steep grade as the trail approaches the General Sherman Tree.

title: Bear Hill Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: General parking is available across the street from the Giant Forest Museum. Accessible parking is available next to the Giant Forest Museum and at the Big Trees Trailhead. Accessible restrooms are available at the Giant Forest Museum.
short_description: The trail follows the old Bear Hill Road and travels under the shade of giant sequoias and mixed conifers. Bear Hill Road is wide and easy to follow with a moderate grade.

title: Pear Lake Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: There are accessible parking spots and accessible flush toilets available at the Wolverton parking lot.
short_description: The Pear Lake Trail is the most challenging of the marked ski trails in Sequoia National Park. The trail climbs steeply through dense fir forest, then ends at the Pear Lake Winter Hut.

title: Alta Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: There are accessible parking spots and accessible flush toilets available at the Wolverton parking lot.
short_description: The Alta Trail descends nearly 1,000 feet from Wolverton to Giant Forest and connects with several other trails. This is a difficult ski with steep terrain and many trees.

title: Crescent Meadow Road Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: General parking is available across the street from the Giant Forest Museum. Accessible parking is available next to the Giant Forest Museum and at the Big Trees Trailhead. Accessible restrooms are available at the Giant Forest Museum.
short_description: The most popular of the Giant Forest’s ski trails, Crescent Meadow Road begins at the west end of the Giant Forest Museum Plaza. The entire route is an unplowed road with gentle to moderate grades and lots of giant sequoias.

title: Sunset Rock Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: There is no parking at the trailhead, but paved paths from various parking areas lead to it. Some paths contain rock steps. General parking is available across the street from the Giant Forest Museum, and is the closest to the trailhead. Accessible parking is available next to the Giant Forest Museum and at the Big Trees Trailhead. Accessible restrooms are available at the Giant Forest Museum.
short_description: This easy trail leads through a mixed-conifer forest of red firs, Jeffrey pines, sugar pines, and incense cedars to a large granite dome. Once there, take a seat on the dome and enjoy the sweeping views of a deep canyon that was carved by the Kaweah River. If you're there for sunset, sit back and enjoy the colorful show! When finished, return on the same trail back to the Giant Forest Museum.

title: Asan Ridge Trail Hike
topics: Ruins;Photography;Coastal Defenses;Battlefields;US Marines;Monuments and Memorials;Pacific Islander Heritage;Trails;Endangered;Rare;World War II
accessibility: The trail is cleared with a grassy and uneven limestone surface. The trail has a section with a concrete staircase.
short_description: Explore Asan Ridge for its historical and natural wonders as well as majestic vistas.

title: Piti Guns Hike
topics: Coastal Defenses;Battlefields;Wars and Conflicts;World War II
accessibility: The cleared trail includes concrete staircase sections as well as uneven limestone surface.
short_description: Hike in a tropical jungle and explore the history of World War II on Guam.

title: Grant Grove Loop Winter Trail
accessibility: In the General Grant Tree parking lot, there is one accessible parking space, accessible flush restrooms, and drinking fountains at the trailhead.
short_description: Visit one of the world's largest living trees. President Coolidge proclaimed the General Grant tree the Nation's Christmas tree in 1926, making it the perfect place to visit for the winter.

title: Boating at Fort Pulaski
accessibility: There is a floating pier with a ramp at the Lazaretto Creek Boat Ramp. Due to tides, the grade of the pier ramp will be outside of ADA regulations. The ramp is the steepest at low tide. Image of the boat ramp from above near low tide.
short_description: How to explore Fort Pulaski's waterways.

title: Panoramic Point and Park Ridge Winter Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: This groomed ski trail follows a paved road for the first 2.5 miles and includes a steep uphill/downhill. At the Grant Grove visitor center, there is one accessible parking space, accessible flush restrooms, and drinking fountains at the trailhead.
short_description: One of the most popular winter trails in this area begins at the village and follows the unplowed road to the top of Park Ridge. Panoramic Point offers spectacular views of the snow-covered mountains in Kings Canyon.

title: North Grove Loop Winter Trail
accessibility: In the General Grant Tree parking lot, there is one accessible parking space, accessible flush restrooms, and drinking fountains at the trailhead.
short_description: The North Grove Loop travels through a magnificent grove of giant sequoias. Skiers will find it easier to follow this loop trail counterclockwise to avoid some of the sharper downhill curves in the road.

title: See Where it All Started - Rancho de Carricitos
accessibility: Historical markers at Carricitos are wheelchair accessible by way of a paved sidewalk off the roadway.
short_description: Visit the site of the first official combat between of the U.S. - Mexican War. On April 24, 1846 Captain Seth Thornton and his 80 dragoons were ambushed by General Anastasio Torrejón and his 1,600 cavalry and infantry troops at Rancho de Carricitos. News of the skirmish was forwarded to President James K. Polk leading him to declare Mexico "has invaded our territory, and shed American blood upon the American soil."

title: Walk the Trails
accessibility: The trails are unpaved and uneven in places. They may also be muddy or covered in snow throughout the year. The trail system generally is downhill towards the river and uphill on the way back.
short_description: Walk the same trails that Frances Perkins did for a respite and inspiration throughout her extraordinary life and career.

title: Hike to Hen Wallow Falls
fee_description: A parking tag is required to park in the Smokies for more than 15 minutes.
accessibility: Hike has steep sections and tree roots across multiple sections of trail.
short_description: Hike 4.3 miles (6.9 km) roundtrip through a hardwood forest with hemlock and rhododendron to a popular 90-foot (27-m) waterfall. This trail includes some steep sections and switchbacks.

title: Wildlife Viewing in the Caldera
fee_description: As of January 1, 2025, a park entrance fee is required to enter Valles Caldera National Preserve.
accessibility: The roads and trails in the preserve are not wheelchair accessible. The pullouts along NM 4 are paved.
short_description: Valles Caldera provides excellent habitat for a wide variety of animals, and there are plenty of opportunities for viewing wildlife like elk, bears, prairie dogs, coyotes, and birds.

title: Valles Caldera Junior Ranger Program
fee_description: As of January 1, 2025, a park entrance fee is required to enter Valles Caldera National Preserve. The Junior Ranger booklet and badge are free.
accessibility: The roads and trails in the preserve are not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Valles Caldera National Preserve currently offers two versions of its Junior Ranger program: an experiential activity booklet designed for in-park completion, and an online program for kids who are unable to visit the park in-person.

title: Valles Caldera Junior Angler Program
fee_description: As of January 1, 2025, a park entrance fee is required to enter Valles Caldera National Preserve. The Junior Angler Program is free and all supplies are provided to participants.
accessibility: The roads and trails in the preserve are not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Get reeled into fishing with the Junior Ranger Let’s Go Fishing! Booklet.

title: Snowshoeing in Valles Caldera
fee_description: As of January 1, 2025, a park entrance fee is required to enter Valles Caldera National Preserve.
accessibility: The trails and roads are not wheelchair accessible and trails are not plowed for snow.
short_description: Winter is a spectacular time to visit Valles Caldera National Preserve. The park has miles of groomed and ungroomed trails for the adventurous snowshoer.

title: Hiking in Valles Caldera
fee_description: As of January 1, 2025, a park entrance fee is required to enter Valles Caldera National Preserve.
accessibility: The roads and trails in the park are not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Hiking routes within Valles Caldera range from flat strolls through montane grasslands to steep climbs on forested lava domes. As this land was a private ranch for over 150 years, the majority of hiking routes follow old logging and ranching roads. Since Valles Caldera is a relatively new National Park Service site, trails are not well-marked, and most trailheads do not yet have signs. For this reason, it is important for hikers to carry a detailed park map and GPS.

title: Cross-Country Skiing in Valles Caldera
topics: Foothills, Plains and Valleys;Forests and Woodlands;Coniferous Forests;Mountains
fee_description: As of January 1, 2025, a park entrance fee is required to enter Valles Caldera National Preserve.
accessibility: The trails and roads are not wheelchair accessible and trails are not plowed for snow.
short_description: Winter is a spectacular time to visit Valles Caldera National Preserve. The park has miles of groomed trails for the adventurous skier.

title: Hike on Chestnut Top Trail
fee_description: A parking tag is required to park in the Smokies for more than 15 minutes.
accessibility: Trail steadily climbs on a sometimes-narrow path with some tree roots and fallen logs.
short_description: Hike 5.6 miles (9 km) roundtrip on a trail that climbs steadily through mixed hardwood forest to a ridgetop where American chestnut trees were once abundant. Fall leaf color and plentiful spring wildflowers remain a draw on this trail.

title: Hike to Kuwohi
fee_description: A parking tag is required to park in the Smokies for more than 15 minutes.
accessibility: Trail is paved but very steep.
short_description: Walk one mile (1.6 km) roundtrip from the Kuwohi (formerly Clingmans Dome) parking area along a steep paved path to an iconic and popular observation tower with panoramic views from the highest peak in the Smokies.

title: Hike to Mount Le Conte on Alum Cave Trail
fee_description: A parking tag is required to park in the Smokies for more than 15 minutes.
accessibility: This trail is steep and rocky, and includes stairs and bridges.
short_description: Hike 10 miles (16.1 km) roundtrip on Alum Cave Trail as it climbs steadily through dense forest to Alum Cave Bluffs and on to the summit of Mount LeConte. This popular but strenuous hike includes stairs, bridges, and some steep and rocky sections of trail.

title: Go Kayaking
accessibility: Accessibility is difficult to these locations. Many launch points may require walking down uneven trail sections, over driftwood, and through sand with no stability infastructure in place.
short_description: Many people come to San Juan Island seeking the adventure of exploring the area by boat. Sea kayaks are very popular for travel among the islands. Operating a small craft on the Salish Sea is fun and exciting, but can also be extremely hazardous when weather conditions become unfavorable. Paddlers must know their equipment, know their limits, obtain a current weather forecast, and respect the ever-changing environment of Puget Sound.

title: Biking on San Juan Island
accessibility: Biking is accesible to those who are able to bike
short_description: Biking is a great way of exploring the island!

title: Fishing at Fort Pulaski
fee_description: Entrance fees apply except at Lazaretto Creek Fishing Pier, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: Fishing from the top of the South Channel Bridge is accessible. The bridge and the ramp to the bridge are paved. Parking is available in pull offs before the bridge. Do not park on the grass. The base of the South Channel Bridge is made of large, rough rocks without an area to stand. Requires climbing down embankment. Lazaretto Creek Fishing Pier is boardwalk, with paved access. The West End Fishing Area is a flat dirt area. There are large, sharp rocks along the waterline. Picture above is the West End Fishing Area.
short_description: Information about fishing in the waterways around Fort Pulaski National Monument.

title: East Auto Tour

accessibility: The road is two miles long and gravel. RV's and vehicles pulling trailers are prohibited.
short_description: The East Auto Tour is two miles long and follows the original Transcontinental railroad grade featuring views of the Wasatch mountains and provides up close examples of railroad construction methods such as earthen fills, railbed cuts, and rock culverts.

topics: Architecture and Building;Asian American Heritage;Commerce;Trade;Engineering;Industry;Laborer and Worker;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Transportation;Trains and Railroads;Westward Expansion

short_description: West Auto Tour

title: Jr Ranger Program
accessibility: Visitors should plan on 30-40 minutes to complete the program. The program is available to all ages.
short_description: Golden Spike is proud to offer the Jr Ranger program for visitors wanting to explore the park and the many stories associated with the railroad.

title: Walk the Earthquake Trail
accessibility: The trail's asphalt pathway was designed to be accessible, and has gentle slopes suitable for wheelchair users. Unfortunately, over the years since it was last paved, depressions have developed in a number of locations, which precludes the pathway from currently meeting criteria for being fully accessible. Some wheelchair users may need assistance to navigate through these degraded sections of the trail. An accessible restroom and two designated parking spaces in a dirt/gravel parking lot are located at the trailhead.
short_description: Discover the geology of the San Andreas Fault on this paved loop nature trail. A fence that was constructed half way around the trail illustrates the 16 feet (3 meters) of displacement that occurred during the infamous 1906 earthquake. The Earthquake Trail begins and ends at the northeast corner of the Bear Valley Trailhead parking lot adjacent to the restrooms for the Bear Valley Picnic Area.

title: Picnic on the Armory Grounds
accessibility: The Springfield Armory grounds have picnic tables located behind the Main Arsenal and by Quarters 1. These tables are accessible by paved asphalt paths that are level and even. The pathway down to the Byers Street and State Street entrance is a steep slope.
short_description: The Armory Grounds are a perfect place to reconnect with nature and escape the hustle and bustle of the urban center, if only for a short time. Find a picnic table, bench or a tree to sit beneath and take a break and enjoy a snack. What do you hear? Do you hear the workers milling about? Horses moving supplies and firearms? Or just the squirrels and birds?

title: Take a Stroll Behind Quarters 1
accessibility: The pathway from the Main Arsenal to Quarters 1 is paved asphalt and is smooth and level. The path goes up to Quarters 1, but behind the land is grassy. As Quarters 1 sits on a hill, it does slope down towards the City of Springfield, but there is a large flat area.
short_description: Take a walk behind Quarters 1 to escape the urban center and reconnect with nature! Behind Quarters 1 there is a large grassy lawn where one can sit and relax and look out over the City of Springfield. The Armory Victory Garden is also located beside Quarters 1; take a look at our garden and all the vegetables and flowers we grow there.

title: Visit the National Park Service Pullman Visitor Center
topics: African American Heritage;Architecture and Building;Immigration;Industry;Laborer and Worker;Labor Movement;Social Movements;Civil Rights;Urban America;Women's History
accessibility: The visitor center is accesible to wheelchairs and has an automatic door opener. There are handicap parking spaces available. Wheelchairs and audio description devices are available upon request at the front desk. Click here for more information on accessibility at Pullman National Historical Park
short_description: The Pullman company became known for creating luxurious train cars, but its workers would help form a lasting legacy through their stories.Start at the Pullman National Historical Park Visitor Center in the Administration-Clock Tower Building to learn more.

title: Explore Historic Carroll Homestead
topics: Architecture and Building;Colonization and Settlement;Farming and Agriculture
accessibility: Accessible parking and portable toilet are available here. The homestead interior and grounds are wheelchair accessible. The grounds are unpaved, and may be unstable after rain or snow. Most activities in the Carroll Homestead ranger program are wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Head towards the west side of the island to visit an example of 1800s island life at Carroll Homestead, a time capsule of early Euro-american settlement before Mount Desert Island became a tourist destination and Acadia National Park came into being.

title: Visit the Park Store
topics: African American Heritage;Animals;Architecture and Building;Colonization and Settlement;Enslavement;Prairies;Piracy and Privateering;Urban America;Wars and Conflicts;War of 1812;Wetlands
accessibility: Service animals are welcome at all sites. Accessibility by site: Acadian Cultural Center , Lafayette Center is wheelchair accessible. Barataria Preserve , Marrero Visitor center is wheelchair accessible. Exhibits include audio exhibits and touchable displays. Environmental education center and trail are wheelchair accessible. The following trails are wheelchair accessible: Visitor Center Trail, Palmetto Trail, Bayou Coquille Trail, and the first third of Marsh Overlook Trail. See the trail map and trail map description to learn more about the preserve trails. Most ranger programs are wheelchair accessible since most programs are given on boardwalk trails. Check with the visitor center at 504-689-3690 ext. 10 for specific program details. Film is closed-captioned. Most of the wayside exhibits are wheelchair accessible. Paved sidewalks run between the visitor center parking area and the Malus-Beauregard House. French Quarter Visitor Center , New Orleans Center is wheelchair accessible. Center includes audio exhibits of local musical styles and special New Orleans dialects and phrases. Prairie Acadian Cultural Center , Eunice Center is wheelchair accessible. Wetlands Acadian Cultural Center , Thibodaux Center is wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Looking for the perfect souvenir? Visit the Park Store! There's one at each of the park's six sites.

title: Watch Old Faithful Geyser Erupt
accessibility: Wide, wheelchair-accessible walkways lead from the Old Faithful Visitor Education Center and all parking areas to Old Faithful Geyser.
short_description: Old Faithful Geyser is the world's best known geyser. Its eruption intervals have varied from 40 to 126 minutes. Find out the eruption times of Old Faithful and other large geysers at the Old Faithful Visitor Education Center, following the @GeyserNPS twitter feed, or using the Geysers app.

duration: Duration varies based on chosen route and conditions.

accessibility: Service Animals Service animals are allowed in national parks. For a definition of a service animal, please see the Americans with Disability Act (ADA) definition. short_description: Meridian Hill Park was designed and built between 1912 and 1936, and has been under the jurisdiction of the National Park Service since 1933.

title: Attend a Ranger Program
fee_description: There is a fee to enter the grounds of Wright Brothers National Memorial.
accessibility: The program is generally accessible. The program will take visitors along paved sidewalks near the visitor center. It will start at the patio, where visitors can sit for the first few minutes. The rest of the program will involve walking and standing, either on the sidewalk or grass, near the reconstructed camp buildings. There is not a lot of shade on the grounds. On hot humid days, heat exhaustion can set in very quickly. Make sure to bring water and sun protection!
short_description: Attend one of the programs offered at Wright Brothers National Memorial

title: Winter Eagle Watching at the Lackawaxen River Access
accessibility: The Lackawaxen River Access is a paved parking area. There are designated parking spots and designated accessible parking spaces. The closest public restroom is located at the parking lot on the Pennsylvania-side of Roebling's Delaware Aqueduct, about half a mile away (a couple minutes away if driving). The parking lot at the aqueduct does have accessible parking spaces available. There is an AED device in the Zane Grey Museum across the street. The Zane Grey Museum is generally open on weekends in January and February during Winter Eagle Watch Programs and from Memorial Day to Labor Day, Thursdays – Sundays.
short_description: Although many eagles call the Upper Delaware River region home during all months of the year, winter is a particularly good time to go bald eagle-watching in the park. Wintering bald eagles visit, increasing the population of eagles in the area. Furthermore, during weekends in January and February, volunteer docents are available at the Lackawaxen River Access to answer questions and promote good “Eagle Etiquette.”

title: Hike the D&H Towpath Trail
accessibility: Although trail is relatively flat, it is not a paved trail. Trail is approximately 0.8 miles and made of dirt, grass, and/or gravel at different sections and is approximately 8 feet wide. Trail may get wet and muddy after rain, snow, and other inclement weather. This is a forested trails so tree roots and fallen branches may also be present of the trail. The parking lot next to trailhead does have an accessible parking space. The connecting trail to the wildlife observation area is made of packed gravel and is relatively flat.
short_description: Enjoy this easy 0.8 mile walking trail that takes you along the Delaware River and remains of the historic Delaware and Hudson (D&H) Canal. This trailhead is adjacent to the historic Roebling Aqueduct, Roebling Aqueduct Tollhouse, and within a few minutes' drive of the Zane Grey Museum, all managed by the National Park Service.

title: Hike the Cobey Pond Trail
topics: Birds;Forests and Woodlands;Deciduous Forests;Lakes;River and Riparian;Scenic Views;Trails;Wetlands
accessibility: The trail starts off at a moderate incline for approximately a fourth of a mile (400m) up to Cobey Pond. The trail up to the pond is gravel and approximately 6-8 feet wide. At Cobey Pond, there is a wooden dock visitors can use. This dock does not have walls or railings. The trail around the pond and back to the trailhead varies from tall grass to dirt and leaf litter and on average is 4-5 feet (1.5m) wide. One may encounter rocks, mud, pools of water, and small gaps in the trail. Total elevation gain is approximately 245 feet (75m).
short_description: This loop trail offers a leisurely stroll around the picturesque Cobey Pond after a moderate incline through the forest from the trailhead to the pond. The trail offers hikers ample opportunities for view wildlife and waterfowl. The trail is located on Pennsylvania Game Lands 316.

title: Hike the Minisink Battleground Park Trail System
topics: Forests and Woodlands;Battlefields;Monuments and Memorials;Rock Landscapes and Features;Trails;American Revolutionary War
accessibility: This is a moderately easy trail which although mostly flat, does have a few moderate inclines depending on which trails you choose to take. Notable inclines include parts of the trail from the parking area to Minisink Monument, and on the Rockshelter Trail to the Minisink Spring. However, major inclines can be avoided by avoiding certain trail paths over others. Trail path is mossy, sometimes with rocks, mud, and tree roots, and is approximately 4 feet wide (1.2m) though it may narrow on some parts of the trails. Accessible parking spots are available at the main parking area.
short_description: Walk this moderately easy, moss-covered loop trail system to catch glimpses of both nature and history. Minisink Battleground Park is the site of the only Revolutionary War battle fought in the Upper Delaware River Valley. Please note Minisink Battleground Park is closed December 1 - April 30. The park is owned and managed by Sullivan County Parks and Recreation.

title: Hike the Mongaup River Trail
topics: Burial, Cemetery and Gravesite;Forests and Woodlands;Deciduous Forests;River and Riparian;Trails
accessibility: The trail is relatively flat with inclines both up and down throughout, resulting in a total elevation gain of approximately 72 feet (22m). The trail varies from 3-6 feet (1-2m) wide and is made of dirt, with obstacles such as muddy areas, rocks, and tree roots. Please be mindful of drop offs, as the path follows the banks of the Mongaup River, whose current can be quite fast with white-water rapids.
short_description: This linear 2-mile (3.2km) trail along the Mongaup River provides a moderate hike with abundant opportunities to view eagles, waterfowl, and wildflowers while listening to the soothing rushing water of the nearby stream. Please note this trail is closed from December 1st - March 31st. This trail is located on land owned and managed by the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation.

title: Hike, cycle, or ride through Fort Ord National Monument
topics: Colonization and Settlement;Explorers and Expeditions;Grasslands;Hispanic American Heritage;Immigration;Latino American Heritage;Migrations;Military;Monuments and Memorials;Native American Heritage;Trails
accessibility: This is a narrow non-motorized dirt road with elevation gain.
short_description: Hike or ride a strenuous 4.5-mile segment that crosses the majestic grasslands of Fort Ord National Monument. The Monument segment is anchored by the Creekside Terrace Trailhead and the Badger Hills Trailhead where restrooms, maps, and interpretive displays are provided. The Creekside Terrace Trailhead has potable water.

title: Hike the Tusten Mountain Trail
topics: Birds;Ruins;Commerce;Forests and Woodlands;Deciduous Forests;Industry;Mining;River and Riparian;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Trails;Wilderness
accessibility: This is a moderately difficult trail with many inclines and steep areas. It is uneven and not a paved trail, starting off as a wide, approximately 10 feet (3m) gravel road from the Ten Mile River Access to the Trailhead, and then switching over to a narrower dirt trail, on average 3-4 feet (1-1.5 m) wide. The trail can get wet and muddy in certain areas, but is also rocky as one progresses up the mountain. Close to the beginning of the trail (going counterclockwise), one will cross a series of simple bridges made of long wood planks placed across ditches, gaps, and/or small gorges. These bridges do not have railings or walls so please walk over them carefully. Other obstacles hikers may encounter include tree roots, downed trees, and drop offs. When snow and ice are present, parts of trail can be slippery. Elevation gain is approximately 500 vertical feet (150m). The trail reaches elevation of over 1120 feet (340m) over sea level.
short_description: This moderately difficult three-mile trail takes you on a loop through historic remains of the Tusten Settlement as you climb to the summit for a magnificent view of the Upper Delaware Valley. Public access to Tusten Mountain Trail is made possible through an agreement with the Conservation Fund.

title: Hike the Damascus Forest Trail
topics: Ruins;Forests and Woodlands;Coniferous Forests;Deciduous Forests;River and Riparian;Trails;Wetlands
accessibility: This is a moderately easy trail that has some inclines. Trail surface is unpaved and varies between grass and dirt as it winds through the forest. Trail width varies from approximately 3 to 5 feet (1-1.5m). Please watch out for obstacles such as tree roots and rocks. At some points on the path, you will have to walk in between openings in crumbling, rock walls. Pit toilet-style bathrooms are available at the southwestern end of the loop. These are not accessible restrooms.
short_description: Enjoy the varied landscape of wetlands, uplands, and old growth forests on this easy loop trail. A large stand of old growth hemlock trees reminds us of the virgin forests that once stood here. This trail is located on land owned and managed by Damascus Township.

title: Tour the Visitor Center
accessibility: Service animals are allowed inside the visitor center. A wheelchair is available for use - ask at the visitor center front desk. The visitor center has an accessible entrance on the west side of the building.
short_description: Start your visit to President William Jefferson Clinton Birthplace Home NHS at the park visitor center with exhibits plus a kiosk with digital vignettes of memorable moments in President Clinton's life as well as the renovation of the Birthplace Home. Browse the Jefferson National Parks Association (JNPA) bookstore for educational products related to this story and gifts to remember your visit to Hope. Stamp your passport book to capture memories from your visit to our site.

title: See Local History Exhibits & Civil War Artifacts

accessibility: Contact the Strasburg Visitor and Information Center with questions about accessibility.
short_description: The Strasburg Museum at Hupp's Hill, inside the Strasburg Visitor and Information Center, displays local history exhibits alongside battlefield artifacts from the Kehoe collection. The museum exhibits and films in the theater tell of the war-torn Shenandoah Valley of 1864: battles fought by soldiers and hardships endured by civilians.

title: Visit the Battlefield Museum
