short_description: Waite & Peirce: Authentic and Exotic Goods features gifts inspired by the bold spirit of Salem’s privateers and offers visitors a unique shopping experience.

title: Picnic Areas
fee_description: Admission to the park is FREE, but for those who qualify, Senior Passes, Military Passes, Access Passes, and Every Kid in a Park passes are available at the visitor center.
accessibility: The Chestnut Picnic Area is wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Catoctin Mountain Park offers many places for individuals to sit down and enjoy a meal under the forest canopy.

title: Park Museum
topics: African American Heritage;Forests and Woodlands;Great Depression;Industry;Laborer and Worker;Indigenous and Native Warrior;Civil War;World War II
fee_description: Visitor Center Parking Lots There is no parking fee. Cost: $0.00
accessibility: The visitor center is ADA accessible.
short_description: Step inside the visitor center to walk through the park museum exhibits.

title: Catoctin Junior Ranger Program
fee_description: The Junior Ranger Program is free and all supplies are provided to participants.
accessibility: The Visitor Center is Wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Come explore Catoctin Mountain Park with our Junior Ranger Book!

title: Orienteering
fee_description: Admission to the park is FREE, but for those who qualify, Senior Passes, Military Passes, Access Passes, and Every Kid in a Park passes are available at the visitor center.
accessibility: The orienteering course is not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: If you would like to practice your orienteering skills, the park maintains courses that are available for public use.

title: Cross-Country Skiing
fee_description: Ski Rentals : Equipment is available for rent in Frederick, Hagerstown and other large cities. Check in the yellow page listings for specialty shops, sporting goods, and outdoor shops. There are no equipment rentals in Catoctin Mountain Park or in Thurmont, MD.
accessibility: Manahan Road under winter conditions is not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Generally, the best skiing is along certain sections of park roads which are closed to vehicular traffic.

title: Catoctin Junior Angler Program
fee_description: The Junior Angler Program is free and all supplies are provided to participants.
accessibility: The Visitor Center is Wheelchair accessible.
short_description: See what it takes to become a Junior Angler!

title: Horse Riding
fee_description: Admission to the park is FREE, but for those who qualify, Senior Passes, Military Passes, Access Passes, and Every Kid in a Park passes are available at the visitor center.
accessibility: The horse trail is not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Public riding is not permitted on any trails in the park other than the designated public horse trail.

title: Visit the 56 Signers of the Declaration of Independence Memorial
accessibility: All memorials are wheelchair-accessible. Handicap parking is available at the World War II and Lincoln Memorials. Metered parking is available throughout the city, including on Constitution Avenue near Constitution Gardens.
short_description: As you walk through Constitution Gardens, walk across the footbridge to Signers Island. The stones of the Memorial to the 56 Signers of the Declaration of Independence could have been tombstones had events turned out differently. Celebrate these men of courage and vision at our nation's founding by paying homage to these 56 American heroes! Granite stones include facsimiles of their signatures, the location of their homes, and their occupations.

title: Charcoal Exhibit Trail
fee_description: Admission to the park is FREE, but for those who qualify, Senior Passes, Military Passes, Access Passes, and Every Kid in a Park passes are available at the visitor center.
accessibility: The charcoal trail is not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: This one-half mile loop trail will take you along several exhibits and displays that will tell the story of the once thriving charcoal making industry on the mountain.

title: Spicebush Trail
fee_description: Admission to the park is FREE, but for those who qualify, Senior Passes, Military Passes, Access Passes, and Every Kid in a Park passes are available at the visitor center.
accessibility: The Spicebush Trail is wheelchair accessible.
short_description: The Spicebush Trail is a short informative walk with wayside panels describing the ever-changing forests at Catoctin Mountain Park.

title: Blue Blazes Whiskey Still Trail
fee_description: Admission to the park is FREE, but for those who qualify, Senior Passes, Military Passes, Access Passes, and Every Kid in a Park passes are available at the visitor center.
accessibility: The blue blazes trail is not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: As you travel along the Blue Blazes creek, interpretive trailside signs explore stream ecology and the history of whiskey production on Catoctin Mountain during the time of Prohibition. The trail concludes at an actual whiskey still.

title: Bird Watching at Fort McHenry
fee_description: So long as birders stay outside of the historic zone, there is no fee to bird watch at Fort McHenry!
accessibility: Many paved paths allow for easy access throughout the park. Benches are frequent so visitors can sit and relax while looking for birds!
short_description: Fort McHenry's water front makes for an ideal birding location. Learn how birders can come enjoy their hobby within the park!

title: Birdwatching - Brown's Farm Trail
fee_description: Admission to the park is FREE, but for those who qualify, Senior Passes, Military Passes, Access Passes, and Every Kid in a Park passes are available at the visitor center.
accessibility: The Brown's Farm Trail is not wheelchair accessible.
short_description: Birds can be observed throughout the entire park, but the secluded nature of the west side makes it ideal for birdwatching.

title: Ride Your Bike at Fort McHenry
topics: Forts;Coastal Defenses;Monuments and Memorials;River and Riparian;Scenic Views;Trails
accessibility: All areas in the park that bikes can be ridden are on paved paths accessible to those who would need to access them.
short_description: Learn how and where to safely enjoy riding bikes at Fort McHenry.

title: Sunset Trail
accessibility: The trail is dirt and gravel with uneven footing. It is not ADA accessible.
short_description: Sunset Trail is the longest trail in Hot Springs National Park, covering approximately 10 miles one-way. Crossing all types of terrain, the trail makes its way through the most remote areas of the park. This trail is divided into three sections: West Mountain (2.8 miles), Sugarloaf Mountain (2.6 miles), and Stonebridge Road (3.8 miles). Sunset Trail can be combined with Hot Springs and North Mountain trails and West Mountain trails to complete a strenuous 15 mile loop hike.

title: Oertel Trail
accessibility: The Oertel Trail is a steep, bumpy gravel trail and is not ADA accessible.
short_description: From downtown, ascend the Stephen's Balustrade (grand staircase) behind the Fordyce Visitor Center to the Grand Promenade and climb the next two sets of steps until you reach the gravel road. Take the road right until you reach an iron gate; the trailhead begins here. Oertel Trail ranges from moderate to very steep grade.

title: Peak Trail
fee_description: The Mountain Tower has a fee if you would like to take an elevator up to the observation deck.
accessibility: The beginning of Peak Trail is paved then turns to gravel. It is a moderate trail: 0.6 mi (1.0 km), 644-1044 ft (196-318 m) elevation, and typical grade of 12.6%.
short_description: Peak Trail leads to the Hot Springs Mountain Tower. The Trail is 0.6 mi (1.0 km) long with an elevation gain of 644 - 1044 ft (196-318 m). It has a 12.6% grade. The trailhead is located near the center of the Grand Promenade. Peak Trail is paved then turns to gravel and connects to many other hiking trails around Hot Springs Mountain.

title: Grand Promenade National Recreation Trail
accessibility: The Grand Promenade is an 8 foot wide paved, brick pathway with a grade of 3.7%.
short_description: This National Recreation Trail is the entry point for many of the Hot Springs and North Mountain trails from downtown.

title: Bicycle Riding
accessibility: With the right equipment, such as adaptive bicycles, the Pullman Trail and paved roads remain accessible for cycling. The paved roads are wide, but maintain a successive incline all the way to the top for at least a mile. Always use caution when cycling near traffic.
short_description: Biking through national parks is a great way to see beautiful scenery and discover new places. Cyclists are allowed and welcome to ride on any of the paved roads in the park. The roads up to North Mountain and West Mountain maintain a progressive incline with moderate traffic, so please use caution and plan accordingly. *Bicycles are not allowed on the Grand Promenade or on the sidewalk in front of Bathhouse Row.

title: Photography in the Park
duration: This activity can take as long, or be as short as you'd like it to be.
accessibility: Photography locations are available all throughout the park. The most accessible locations, located in downtown Hot Springs are along Bathhouse Row and at Whittington Park. Bathhouse Row has a paved, 6 foot wide side walk that cirlces the Bathhouses, with a maximum grade of 3.7%. Whittington Park has a flat, gravel pathhway that is 1.2 miles long with a 0.6% grade.
short_description: Photography is an important part of national park history. Photographers took pictures to show why special places needed protection. People were able to see how beautiful and unique park landscapes were even if they could not visit them in person. Today, professional and amateur photographers alike travel from around the world to capture scenic and historic vistas.

title: Johnny Horn Trail
topics: African American Heritage;Birds;Ruins;Architecture and Building;Photography;Burial, Cemetery and Gravesite;Enslavement;Plantations;Industry;Mills;Natural Sounds;Oceans;Coral Reefs;Churches;Missions;Scenic Views;The Tropics;Trails
time_of_day: It is best to enjoy this trail in the early morning or late afternoon hours to avoid the heat.
accessibility: The trail is steep and rocky in places. The first portion of the trail is a moderate climb and leads to great views and historic sites. Visitors may chose to just do this first portion and then enjoy the cool clear water of Leinster Bay.
short_description: This strenuous trail leads to the remains of some beautiful stone historic sites and incredible views.

title: L'Esperance Trail
accessibility: This trail is not considered accessible.
short_description: L'Esperance Trail follows a historic Danish road passing ruins of some of the earliest plantations established on St. John. View the island's only baobab, a sacred tree species that was brought to the Caribbean by enslaved Africans. From trailhead to the beach is about 2.6 miles one way. Much of the trail faces west and lacks tree shade so be sure to wear sun protection and a hat.

title: Raft or Kayak the Alagnak River
accessibility: The National Park Service does not maintain any public facilities along the Alagnak River. However, there are several lodges located on private land along the Alagnak Wild River corridor.
short_description: On the Alagnak, serenity and wildlife viewing opportunities abound for those lazily floating the river while Class III rapids offer exciting trips for rafters.

title: Francis Bay Trail
accessibility: The boardwalk to the salt pond viewing platforms is wheelchair accessible. The rest of the trail is uneven and rocky. There is a steep climb from the parking lot at the Francis Sugar Factory to the beach and boardwalk. Those looking for easier access should park at the beach end of the trail.
short_description: Francis Bay Trail starts at the Francis Bay Sugar Factory. It continues past the Mary's Point Estate house and around a salt pond. The dry tropical forest and salt pond provide an excellent opportunity to view birds. The lower portion of the trail is an accessible boardwalk that continues through the mangroves to the two viewing platforms.

title: Walnut Canyon Overlook Trail
accessibility: Trail is narrow and steep.
short_description: This short 180 yards (165 m) paved walkway provides great views of Walnut Canyon.

title: Become a Biscayne Junior Ranger
topics: Animals;Alligators or Crocodiles;Birds;Fish;Estuaries and Mangroves;Oceans;Coral Reefs;The Tropics
accessibility: A ranger or volunteer will be happy to help you earn your badge.
short_description: Join Diego the dolphin, Peter the panther and Aleesha the alligator in exploring three South Florida parks (Big Cypress National Preserve, and Biscayne and Everglades National Park). Pick up a booklet at the park visitor center and complete the required activities to earn a badge. Complete the entire book and earn three badges plus an exclusive South Florida junior ranger patch!

title: Hike to Avalanche Lake

accessibility: The first half mile of the trail to Avalanche Lake is the wheelchair-accessible nature trail called the Trail of the Cedars. Beyond that, the trail becomes steeper, rocky, and more challenging.
short_description: Hiking to Avalanche Lake provides an excellent introduction to Glacier.

title: Juniper Ridge Trail
accessibility: Trail is narrow, rocky, and steep in places.
short_description: Enjoy the Chihuahuan Desert in a serene landscape along this 3.5 mile (5 km) trail.

title: Old Guano Trail
accessibility: Trail is narrow and rocky.
short_description: This 3.7 miles (6km) trail descends the escarpment, ending at the White's City campground.

fee_description: The John Muir National Historic Site is free to all visitors.
accessibility: John Muir National Historic Site Here at John Muir NHS we are committed to accessibility. Please contact us if you have any great ideas! Physical/Mobility: The John Muir visitor center offers accessible restrooms. An easy access path offers a less steep route for visitors to reach the Strentzel-Muir house. For visitors who are unable to walk to the house, a ranger will gladly provide transportation via a golf cart. A wheelchair lift allows access to the home's first floor. The wheelchair lift has a 500-lb combined weight limit for each person and his or her wheelchair. A non-motorized wheelchair is available for use on a first-come, first-served basis. Motorized scooters are not permitted in the Strentzel-Muir house or the Martinez Adobe due to the hazards of uneven surfaces and to protect the integrity of these historic buildings. The first floor of the Martinez Adobe and Juan Bautista De Anza National Historic Trail exhibit is also accessible from the south side. ADA approved picnic tables are available as well. There is a video of the second floor of the Muir home, which can be played by the staff, on request, in the Muir home dining room. Deaf/Hearing Loss: The park provides audio listening devices and audio description for the park film. The main park film is also closed-captioned. Blind/Low Vision: The main park brochure is available in braille, please inquire at the front desk for a copy that can be borrowed. Because we do not have a sign language interpreter on staff, please contact the park with your request at least two weeks in advance of your visit, or when you’re making your tour reservation. short_description: The Muir/Strentzel home is located at the main park site and is within walking distance from the visitor center.

title: Strentzel/Muir Gravesite Tour
accessibility: The Muir/Strentzel Gravesite is wheelchair accessible, with some uneven ground in places. Please contact the park for more information.
short_description: The Muir/Strentzel gravesite is not located on the main property of the John Muir National Historic Site.

title: Fishing at Gateway
fee_description: This is typically a free activity. However, parking permits are required to fish after hours throughout the park and in other areas at all time. More information about these permits can be found here .
accessibility: Service animals are allowed throughout the park. Accessible parking is available throughout the park.
short_description: Visitors are able to fish at many sites throughout Gateway. A fishing/parking permit is required after hours throughout the park. There are also some sites that require permits at all time. Visit our fishing page to learn where you need a parking permit and how to purchase the permit.

title: Picnicking At Monocacy
accessibility: Picnic tables are located in flat grassy areas near the parking areas at the Visitor Center and Gambrill Mill. At Thomas and Worthington the picnic tables are near the houses and accessed via a gravel farm road.
short_description: Add a picnic to your exploration of the battlefield. Monocacy National Battlefield has picnic tables at several locations throughout the park.

title: Visit The Sculptor's Studio
accessibility: The Sculptor's Studio is wheelchair accessible. Accessible restrooms and drinking fountain are available on the lower level of the studio via an elevator. Parking is available outside the Sculptor's Studio for those unable to access the Sculptor's Studio using the Presidential Trail. Please talk to a park ranger at an information desk to make arrangements for access to the studio parking area. Service dogs, as defined by the Americans with Disabilities Act requirements , are permitted to accompany visitors with disabilities inside the Sculptor's Studio.
short_description: Visit the Sculptor's Studio to learn more about Gutzon Borglum, his scale model and the process of carving Mount Rushmore.

title: Shop at the Park Store

accessibility: The visitor center is a fully accessible building. Parking Accessible parking is available. Service animals Only service animals that have been individually trained to perform specific tasks for the benefit of persons with disabilities are allowed in the park and in the visitor center.
short_description: The park store is operated by Western National Parks Association, an official non-profit partner of the National Park Service dedicated to supporting the educational mission of Guadalupe Mountains National Park. The park store has a wide range of books, maps, travel guides, and other items available for retail sale. These products complement the interpretive themes you experience when visiting the park. The park store is located in the Pine Springs Visitor Center.

title: Hikes at the Worthington Farm
topics: Animals;Birds;Architecture and Building;Farming and Agriculture;Forests and Woodlands;Deciduous Forests;Trails;Civil War
accessibility: The three hiking trails on the Worthington Farm vary in width and experience significant changes in elevation. The trails lead through wooded areas where tree roots are sometimes exposed. Animals occasionally create burrows along the trails that can create tripping hazards. The trails are dirt paths.
short_description: Take a hike at Worthington Farm! Three trails at Worthington Farm provide options for exploring.

title: Walk the Trails at the Barataria Preserve
topics: Animals;Alligators or Crocodiles;Birds;Fish;Tortoises and Turtles;Estuaries and Mangroves;Forests and Woodlands;Geology;Lakes;Natural Sounds;Scenic Views;Trails;Wetlands;Marshes;Swamps;Wilderness
accessibility: The following trails are wheelchair accessible: Visitor Center Trail, Palmetto Trail, Bayou Coquille Trail, and the first third of Marsh Overlook Trail. See the trail map and trail map description to learn more about the preserve trails.
short_description: Want to experience Louisiana's wetlands? Walk the trails at the Barataria Preserve.

title: Walk the Canyon Nature Trail
fee_description: There is no cost to hike this trail.
accessibility: At the East trail head there are two steps leading up to the trail. To avoid any steps, park at the Swinging Bridge picnic area and walk through the picnic area to access the trail on that side. The trail is paved and has benches along the way for rest. There are places where the trail has worn down and is less smooth.
short_description: Take a walk along the American Fork river on the north side of the canyon. This side of the canyon features wildlife and plants not found on the south side. There are several interpretive signs along the trail and benches to rest on. You can also view the cave entrance roughly 1,000 feet higher and across the canyon using an installed scope.

title: Shop at the Arch Store
accessibility: The store is accessible.
short_description: Find the perfect souvenir and support Gateway Arch National Park with your purchases!

title: Night Skies at Cape Lookout
accessibility: The easiest to reach stagazing location is the parking lot in front of the Harkers Visitor Center and the parking lot for the picnic area across the road from the visitor center. Both areas are level, paved and have paved side walks. Restrooms, including handicapped stalls, are available in both areas. The lights in the restrooms are motion activated at night. Restrooms remain open until 10:00 pm and then automatically lock. A release button inside on the wall to the left of the door allows anyone who was still inside to leave after the locks are engaged. The lights in the parking lot remain off after dark to allow for stargazing. To retain your night vision, use a flashlight with a red light if you need it to move around after dark. If a special event is scheduled after dark in the visitor center, the parking lot lights will be on until after that event ends, then the lights will be turned off for the rest of the night. If out on the barrier islands, please be aware that there are no hard surfaces on the island. Mobility assistance, such as a wheelchair or scooter, will need to be able to handle the deep sand of the beach. The beaches and sand trails for vehicles are uneven and the sand may make walking difficult.
short_description: Cape Lookout National Seashore is a sanctuary for natural darkness on the East coast of the United States. Take this chance to stargaze, and experience the half of the park that many of us miss - nighttime.

title: Fossil Butte Nature Trail
accessibility: This dirt trail is a 1.5 mile loop where you gain 300 feet in elevation. The trail begins at approximately 7000 feet. The trail is generally only wide enough for a single file line.
short_description: This 1.5 mile (2.4 km) loop trail winds through sagebrush steppe and aspen groves. The signs discuss the ecosystems of the park and geology's effect on the plants that grow in the park.

title: Muir Woods Birdwatching
fee_description: There is an entrance fee to Muir Woods National Monument. In addition, parking reservations are required.
accessibility: Accessible Features Designated Accessible Parking Assistive Listening Devices Accessible Restrooms Segments of Accessible Trails Braille Brochure and Trail Map Large Print Brochure Accessible Cafe and Gift Shop Usable Visitors Center Audio Described Brochures and Waysides American Sign Language Orientation Videos Click here to download an audio described version of the Muir Woods Brochure. Service Animals Service Animals, as recognized by the Americans with Disabilities Act, are allowed: Service animals are defined as animals that are individually trained to do work or perform tasks for people with disabilities. Examples of such work or tasks include guiding people who are blind, alerting people who are deaf, pulling a wheelchair, alerting and protecting a person who is having a seizure, reminding a person with mental illness to take prescribed medications, calming a person with Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) during an anxiety attack, or performing other duties. Service animals are working animals, not pets. The work or task a dog has been trained to provide must be directly related to the person’s disability. Animals whose sole function is to provide comfort or emotional support do not qualify as service animals under the ADA. For more information on the DOJ ADA Revised Service Animal Regulations, please click here . Upon Arrival As you arrive at Muir Woods, proceed to the main parking lot follow the signs to the accessible parking stalls located closest to the Visitor Center and park entrance. Accessible restrooms are located across from the parking stalls. The surface material within the entry plaza is a compacted mix of recycled asphalt and dirt. The surface is firm and stable. There are several accessible benches located in the entry plaza. In the Park Once you arrive, head towards the Visitor's Center. Here is where you can request assistive listening devices for our Ranger Led Tours and Mp3 players containing an audio description of the Muir Woods Brochure and waysides along the Main Trail. The Visitors Center also provides a copy of the Muir Woods Brochure in Braille along with a Braille Trail Map. After stopping at the Visitors Center, follow the raised accessible boardwalk. This boardwalk is part of the Muir Woods Main Trail. If you follow the raised boardwalk to the right it will lead to an accessible gift shop, café and restroom facility. Signage is provided. If you choose to continue into the Redwood Forest, the accessible boardwalk will continue for several hundred feet to the Pinchot Tree Area. There are several informational waysides along the boardwalk. If you proceed past the boardwalk you will encounter an asphalt trail which is usable; however, it contains potholes and severe cracks due to heaving tree roots. As funding and resources allow, we will continue to replace the existing asphalt with an accessible raised boardwalk.
short_description: Birdwatching in Muir Woods

title: Hiking The Blackberry Trail
accessibility: This trail approximately two feet wide with a fine gravel surface and a maximum grade of ten percent.
short_description: Looking to experience the natural surroundings of the Black Hills? Try hiking the Blackberry Trail.

title: View Landmarks along the Santa Fe Trail
fee_description: Fees being charged will vary by location. Please check with the individual site for more information.
accessibility: Accessibility information will vary by location. Please check with the individual site for more specific information. Services animals are allowed at all locations.
short_description: There has been a lot of change since the mid 1800's. Landmarks are an opportunity to view the trail similar to the way the traders did. Some landmarks may sit in their original viewshed, giving you a real experience of stepping back to the trail days. Other landmarks may be surrounded by the 21st century and provide a chance to think about how things have changed in 200 years.

title: Hike the Cave Trail
fee_description: There is no fee for hiking the trail.
accessibility: Although the trail is paved it is not wheelchair accessible due to the grade and steep dropoffs along the cliff edges.
short_description: The Timpanogos Cave Trail is 1.5 miles each way and gains 1,100 vertical feet. Hike past thousands of years of geologic history while enjoying breathtaking vistas and the natural sounds of the park. Plan on approximately 2-2.5 hours roundtrip.

title: Sacajawea’s Rest Park
topics: Arts;Sculpture;Colonization and Settlement;Explorers and Expeditions;Forts;Military;Monuments and Memorials;Native American Heritage;Trails;Westward Expansion;Women's History
short_description: This statue of Sacajawea and her son, Jean Baptiste, was made by artist Jim Demetro. Sacajawea, the only woman involved in the expedition, is an important figure in American history. The statue is located at Sacajawea’s Rest Park, a tiny park located between two buildings in Darby, Montana. The artist also made an identical statue at Fort Clatsop, Lewis and Clark National Historical Park, located in Oregon and Washington.

title: Explore L'Hermitage
topics: African American Heritage;Colonization and Settlement;Enslavement;Farming and Agriculture;Plantations;Scenic Views
fee_description: No fee.
accessibility: The parking area is gravel. Trail surfaces are mowed grass or gravel. Paths are fairly smooth and flat; however, they have not been improved to comply with slope and grade for accessible trails. With the exception of the stone barn, buildings are not open to the public. Audio descriptions of buildings and the farm are available in the NPS app.
short_description: Explore the late 18th century slave plantation known as L'Hermitage.

title: Historic Weapons Demonstrations
topics: Military;Infantry and Militia;Wars and Conflicts;French and Indian War
fee_description: There are no entrance or fees for public interpretive programs at Fort Necessity
accessibility: The trail to the program area and the demontration area is wheelchair/stroller accessible. The viewing area for the weapon firing demonstration is level but bumpy lawn inside Fort Necessity. Patrons with sensitive hearing, aversions to loud noises, pets, small children, or PTSD should be aware the historic weapons produce loud explosive noise and may want to a experience it from a distance. Demonstrators will give a warning before firing.
short_description: Black powder weapons demonstrations are given daily throughout the summer at Fort Necessity as staffing permits.

title: Limberlost
fee_description: An entrance fee is required to get into Shenandoah National Park.
accessibility: Although pets are not allowed on Limberlost Trail, service animals are welcome. Limberlost is a fully accessible trail. Length: 2338.3 yards/2138.1 meters Surface Type: primarily crushed greenstone Typical Tread Width: 5 feet/1.5 meters Minimum Tread Width: 2.7 feet/.8 meters Typical Running Slope: 3.5% Maximum Running Slope: 10.3% Typical Cross Slope: 1.6% Maximum Cross Slope: 5.0%
short_description: Limberlost Parking Area (mile 43) | An ADA accessible path through the forest with mountain laurel in the springtime and an example of a columnar jointing geological feature. This hike is also a designated TRACK Trail, featuring a self-guided brochure designed for kids.

title: Blackrock Summit
fee_description: An entrance fee is required to get into Shenandoah National Park.
accessibility: This trail does not meet ADA accessibility guidelines.
short_description: Blackrock Parking Area (mile 84.4) | A short hike to a viewpoint on top of a rocky talus slope with incredible views of the Shenandoah Valley, Massanutten Mountain, and beyond. This hike is also a designated TRACK Trail, featuring a self-guided brochure designed for kids.

title: Walk Long Logs Trail
accessibility: The first half-mile of this trail is paved and suitable for mobility equipment and strollers. Strollers may be negotiated on the loop, but it is not recommended for most wheelchairs and other mobility equipment due to its narrow turns, grade, and rough surface. Tread width: 85 in (216 cm), min 50 in Grade: 3.5%, max 20.5% Cross Slope: 2.9%, max 17.4%
short_description: Explore this ancient log jam at the base of purple and gray badlands along a paved half-mile loop.

title: Hike the Western Ridge Trail
accessibility: The Western Ridge Trail crosses over sections that are paved, wider to accommodate horse travel and some that are extremely narrow and are rated as being challenging and not accessible.
short_description: The Western Ridge Trail has green trail markings and runs the length of the park north to south.

title: Walk the Tawa Trail
accessibility: Hard-surface, wide trail, plenty of places to turn around as needed. Meets standards for outdoor developed areas. Typical grade 2.3% with grades up to 8.3% Typical Cross Slope: 2% Max Cross Slope: 5% Typical Tread Width: 60 in (152.4 cm) No obstacles
short_description: Enjoy the tranquility of the grassland as the paved trail leads you to scenic Tawa Point. The 1.2-mile one way Tawa Trail is a perfect place to stretch your legs after a long road trip.

title: Become a Joshua Tree Junior Ranger
accessibility: The Junior Ranger booklet can be completed in many different sections of the park with varying degrees of accessibility. Information on specific areas can be found at visitor centers or on the park's accessibility page .
short_description: Become a Junior Ranger at Joshua Tree National Park.

title: Enjoy Horseback Riding
accessibility: Up to the individual's knowledge and abilities.
short_description: Bring your own horse and take a ride into the backcountry.

title: Walk the Painted Desert Rim Trail
accessibility: Tread width: 62 in (158.6 cm), min 60 in (152.4 cm) Grade: 6.3%, max 25.6% Cross Slope: 3.8%, max 16.2%T his trail does not have stairs, but the waterbars and dirt-gravel surface may make this trail unsuitable for strollers or mobility devices.
short_description: This unpaved trail winds 1-mile round trip through the rim woodland, a place for chance encounters of many species of plants and animals and spectacular views of the Painted Desert.

title: Walk Puerco Pueblo Trail
accessibility: Suitable for strollers and various mobility equipment (power and manual), except on short trail spurDepending on the individual, most of this trail is accessible for mobility devices. The surface is hard, paved or graveled. Exhibits have proper contrast for visibility challenges.
short_description: The 3/4 -mile paved Puerco Pueblo Trail features the remnants of a hundred room masonry pueblo.

title: Walk Crystal Forest Trail
accessibility: Tread width: 71 in (179.8 cm), min 65 in (165.1 cm) Grade: 5.2%, max 22.5% Cross Slope: 2.2%, max 11.3% Depending on the individual, most of this trail is accessible for mobility devices. The surface is hard, paved or graveled. Exhibits have proper contrast for visibility challenges.
short_description: Walk Crystal Forest Trail for one of the best opportunities to experience the petrified wood deposits as it loops through rolling gray and purple badlands.

title: Walk Blue Mesa Trail
accessibility: Most of this trail is not accessible for mobility devices. Steep grade near beginning of trail. The surface is hard, paved or graveled. Exhibits have proper contrast for visibility challenges.
short_description: This 1-mile alternately paved and gravel trail loop offers the unique experience of hiking among banded badland hills of bentonite clay as well as petrified wood.

title: Explore at the Paleo Exhibits at Rainbow Forest Museum
accessibility: The museum is accessible for mobility devices and has a push button entrance. There is a ramp in the front and level in the back. The exhibits have proper contrast to help with visibility challenges. Staff is available for questions.
short_description: Explore the paleontology exhibits at Rainbow Forest Museum.

title: Become a BARK Ranger!
accessibility: Service animals are welcome everywhere in the park where the public can go.
short_description: As long as you both follow the BARK Ranger rules, you can take your leashed dog, cat, or other pet almost everywhere you can go in the park.

title: Go Geocaching
accessibility: Some of the caches are accessible for various challenges, others are not. Should be attached to the geocache description.
short_description: Go geocaching. There are multiple caches in the park including traditional and virtual.

title: Eat Lunch at Aztec Ruin's Picnic Area
accessibility: Paved pathway leads to two tables that are accessible.
short_description: Enjoy a picnic in the shade.

title: Aztec West Great House Loop
accessibility: Much of the trail is paved. Steep steps lead into the Great Kiva. One section of the trail leads through rooms with low doorways and dirt floors.
short_description: A half mile long loop following a mostly paved trail through the ancestral Pueblo Great House.

title: Watch Wildlife
accessibility: Most overlooks are accessible for mobility challenges with large paved spaces.
short_description: Watching wildlife is a seasonal activity, but just in that the species to watch change, particularly in birdwatching.

title: Strenuous Hike Across the Crater Floor
accessibility: This trail is extremely long and steep. While the trailheads have accessible parking, this trail is not recommended for who may require assistance.
short_description: Experienced hikers can "thru" hike the crater from Keoneheʻeheʻe (Sliding Sands) Trailhead, across the crater floor, and out to Halemauʻu Trailhead. This hike is extremely strenuous and should only be undertaken by individuals who are equipped for a wilderness environment.

title: Birdwatching in the Park
accessibility: Birdwatching often requires moments of quiet observation and keen listening. Most birders will often hear a bird before they see one. The two most accessible places for birdwatching are along the Grand Promenade, which is at least a 6 feet wide, .5 mile paved brick pathway with a grade of 3.7%; and, Whittington Park which offers a 1.2 mile flat, gravel loop trail with a grade of 0,6%, and offers many benches for sitting.
short_description: Birds are everywhere. They soar overhead, flit through branches, walk on the ground, and swim in the water. From the tiny calliope hummingbird to the gigantic California condor, a great diversity of birds finds a home in the national parks. Even more species pass through during migration. Casual observers and hardcore birders alike can experience the joy of birds and birding in a national park.

title: Become an Aztec Ruins Junior Ranger
accessibility: The Junior Ranger activities can be completed in an accessible manner.
short_description: Aztec Ruins National Monument offers a Junior Ranger program for the young and young at heart. Upon completion, participants will earn their Junior Ranger badge. Junior Ranger worksheets are available at the visitor center.

title: Watch Bears at Brooks Camp
accessibility: Wile most areas around Brooks Camp and the trail to Brooks Falls are wheelchair accessible, they are unpaved and frequently muddy. The walk to Brooks Falls can be arduous for some people with limited mobility. A number of wheelchairs are available to borrow from the Brooks Camp Visitor Center.
short_description: Brooks Camp is renowned for its remarkable bear viewing opportunities.

title: See the Battle of Lake Erie
