title: Catch a Historic Weapons Demonstrations
topics: Maritime - Military;Military;Artillery;Indigenous and Native Warrior;Infantry and Militia;US Army;US Marines;US Navy;War of 1812
accessibility: Demonstrations are giving on the lawn around the Memorial. Sidewalks can get visitors close but sometimes not to the demonstration. The talks giving with small arms demonstrations are often given on the steps of the Memorial between upper and lower plazas. To get there a visitor would need to climb approximately 5 steps to get on lower plaza.
short_description: Come see how men dressed and fought in the War of 1812.

title: Historic Alley Mill Talk
accessibility: An accessible parking location exists to the west of the main parking lot. To access it follow the visitor information arrow that leads to the General Store Visitor Center. The trail to Alley Mill is accessible but a cobblestone walkway and wooden bridge crossing are present. No restrooms are available at Alley Mill. Alley Mill's 1st floor is accessible to wheelchairs but turning radius is hindered by milling equipment.
short_description: Tour the iconic and historic Alley Roller Mill at Alley Spring. Alley Mill is rumored to be the most photographed mill in the state and perhaps the nation.

title: Walk in the Last Footsteps of Meriwether Lewis
accessibility: The part of this trail up to the Old Trace is paved, but slightly rough. The section of the Old trace is a packed natural historic trail. The monument is along a road. The interpretive exhibits are tactile, but there is no audio description of the text.
short_description: Follow last footsteps of explorer Meriwether Lewis on a section of the Old Natchez Trace and visit his burial site. This self-guide tour will take you a little over half a mile in an easy loop along a trail with interpretive exhibits, to the historic Old Trace, to his burial place and monument, then back past the Information Cabin at the Grinders Stand site where Meriwether Lewis died.

title: View the Night Sky at Split Mountain
accessibility: Stargazing sites are available from any paved overlook and parking area in the monument. The location of our designated night sky viewing area is along a levely paved path.
short_description: Dinosaur has been recognized as an International Dark Sky Park by the International Dark Skies Association. Much of the monument provides opportunities to view the night skies. The Split Mountain Campground has a designated night sky viewing area and is where the monument hosts night sky viewing programs.

title: Earn Your Junior Ranger Badge
topics: Colonization and Settlement;Enslavement;Estuaries and Mangroves;Plantations;Colonial/European Contact Conflicts
fee_description: A free program
accessibility: A screen readable version of the program is posted on our website and rangers are happy to accommodate different learning modalities the best we are able.
short_description: Complete the activity book and earn a badge. Our park offers a chance to earn two different badges, one for Timucuan Preserve and another for Fort Caroline.

title: Take a Self-Guided Tour of Giant Logs
accessibility: Hard paved or graveled surface Tread width: 57 in (145.6 cm), min 48 in (121.9 cm) Grade: 4.8%, max 19.1% Cross Slope: 2.5%, max 13.4% Booklet with text has good constrast. Audio is not available.
short_description: Take a self-guided tour of Giant Logs, one of the highest concentration of large, colorful petrified logs.

title: Paddling Mt. Hersey to Woolum
accessibility: River accesses are gravel. No ADA accessible ramps at access locations.
short_description: This reach provides numerous bluffs, shoals and pools along the way.

title: Join A Ranger
topics: Animals;Birds;Archeology;Photography;Canyons and Canyonlands;Climate Change;Explorers and Expeditions;Plateaus and Mesas;Forests and Woodlands;Fossils and Paleontology;Geology
accessibility: We are continually working to upgrade facilities for accessibility and to improve park access for all visitors. While not all facilities are fully accessible, park rangers are happy to assist any visitor with special needs. If you have comments or suggestions about facilities, services, or programs, please let us know. Learn more about accessibility at Big Bend National Park Accessibility - Big Bend National Park
short_description: Join a Park ranger for a guided hike, talk, or evening program. Discover the amazing stories behind the scenery of Big Bend.

title: View the Alcatraz Fire Engine
accessibility: The exhibit features large text, which is also reproduced here in the NPS App.
short_description: Restored in 2003, this historic Diamond T Fire Engine can be viewed in the garage of the Quartermaster Building.

title: Tour the Cellhouse
fee_description: The Cellhouse Tour costs $12, which is included in the price of your ferry ticket.
accessibility: The Cellhouse Tour is available in American Sign Language on a hand held device. An audio decrescribed version of the tour is also available. The audio described tour includes 12 strategically placed tactile markers and a tactile replica of the bar spreader used in the famous escape. Transcripts of the tour are available in all the available languages and Braille.
short_description: Listen to the voices of formerly incarcerated men and the correctional officers who guarded them, as they tell you the stories of United States Penitentiary: Alcatraz. This award winning tour guides you through the Alcatraz Cellhouse and is available in eleven languages.

title: Paddle and Fish Loon Lake
accessibility: Loon Lake is equipped with accessible parking, restrooms, picnic shelters, and has an accessible canoe/kayak launch system where boaters can board, launch and disembark from a watercraft safely and easily. The ADA-compliant, floating dock system includes an accessible transfer system along with an accessible canoe/kayak launch system.
short_description: Have a picnic on the shore of one of the park’s tranquil inland lakes. A big lake with a sandy bottom, Loon Lake has a new fishing pier and accessible kayak launch.

title: Float the Platte and Crystal Rivers
accessibility: Platte River Picnic Area is equipped with accessible parking, restrooms, picnic shelters, and a fish cleaning station, raised grills, and a hardened surface river walk. Some assistance may be necessary on the ramps to the river walk and to access boats on the river's edge. Platte River Point beach and picnic area is equipped with accessible parking, restrooms with running water, accessible dressing rooms and raised charcoal grills.
short_description: Canoe, kayak, or float these calm rivers. Rent equipment near either launch site if you don’t have your own. Great for kids!

title: Glasshouse Ruins
accessibility: Access is by way of parking lot down a gradual slope that is a sidewalk and then compacted earth. Entry to this building is through doorway and out the exit.
short_description: Site of the original glassworks. Site is self guiding with waysides and items to see within the building.

title: Island Loop Drive
accessibility: Walking and bicycling is along side of roadway.
short_description: Jamestown has a one-way three/five mile scenic loop drive of the Island. This loop drive is open to pedestrians, bicycles and motor vehicles. Safety issues prohibit buses, motor homes or vehicles over 5-tons from using the Loop Drive. From the Historic Jamestowne parking lot, follow the signs to the loop drive. All state and local traffic regulations apply.

title: Glasshouse
accessibility: Glasshouse is accessible by way of parking lot and down a gradual slope to the demonstration area. Restrooms are located at the parking lot.
short_description: Visitors can see the remains of the original furnaces used by those early glassblowers and watch as modern glassblowers produce wine bottles, pitchers, candleholders and various other glass objects.

title: Salomon/Honeymoon Bays
topics: Coasts, Islands and Atolls;Oceans;Coral Reefs;The Tropics
accessibility: hhh
short_description: Salomon/Honeymoon Bay - These two white-sand beaches can be accessed by a short hike from Lind Point Trail that begins at the Visitor Center parking lot, from the trailhead at the Virgin Islands National Park sign off North Shore Road, or by boat.

title: Whale watch from Muir Beach Overlook
accessibility: Avoid the overlook trail if you're scared of heights. Cliffs along the Rocky Point coast are isolated and very dangerous. Use caution when hiking Cell phone coverage is not reliable. Rescue crews are further away. The overlook picnic site is scenic but windy, so remember to carry layers and hold on to your paper plates! Accessible Features Designated Accessible Parking Accessible Vault Toilet Accessible Picnic Tables Tactile / Braille Topographic Model Accessible Pathways Upon Arrival There are two designated accessible parking spaces located within the parking lot. Inside the Park Adjacent to one of the designated accessible parking spaces is an accessible vault toilet. There is an accessible outdoor route leading to the information kiosk. Past the information kiosk you will find a large scale tactile topographic model which contains Braille labels. There is also a series of information panels. There are several accessible picnic tables all located on accessible outdoor routes. Some portions of the trails are generally accessible while others contain very steep terrain and stairs
short_description: Whale Watch from Muir Beach Overlook

title: Fishing at Mount Rainier National Park
duration: Fishing can take a few hours to multiple days if combined with a longer camping or backpacking trip.
fee_description: Park entrance fee required. No permit or license required for fishing.
accessibility: Access to water features within the park varies, but usually involves some initial on-trail travel, then off-trail travel to approach the water source. Trails are usually narrow, un-paved, and are often broken by tree roots or other obstacles. River and lake shores are often surrounded by dense forest, and ground can be soft and marshy or can have steep or rocky drop-offs to reach the water level.
short_description: Mount Rainier is not known for fishing, but many lakes were historically stocked with non-native fish. Anglers can play an important role in protecting native fish populations by following fishing regulations and reducing numbers of non-native fish.

title: Hike Coal Vein Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information .
accessibility: Coal Vein Trail is an unpaved trail which includes uneven footing, steep stairs, and potential slip hazards. Hikers should keep away from steep cliff edges. Proper footwear is recommended. Service animals are allowed, but must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet.
short_description: Take a hike on this 0.8-mile loop and learn about the geology of Theodore Roosevelt National Park.

title: Hike Wind Canyon Trail
topics: Canyons and Canyonlands;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Trails
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information .
accessibility: Wind Canyon Trail is an unpaved trail which includes uneven footing, steps, and potential slip hazards. There is a very small seating area approximately halfway along the trail. Proper footwear is recommended. Service animals are allowed, but must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet.
short_description: Wind Canyon trail is a short, moderate-difficulty trail that rewards hikers with incredible views of the Little Missouri river and the surrounding badlands.

title: Biking at Ocmulgee Mounds
topics: Animals;Alligators or Crocodiles;Birds;Fish;Tortoises and Turtles;Forests and Woodlands;Deciduous Forests;Native American Heritage;River and Riparian;Scenic Views;Trails;Transportation;Roads, Routes and Highways;Wetlands
accessibility: All biking trails are paved. The grade varies from level to steep throughout the park.
short_description: Biking is a great way to experience Ocmulgee Mounds while getting in some exercise.

title: Hike Boicourt Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information .
accessibility: The Boicourt Trail is approximately 0.2 miles long and 3 feet wide. It is fully paved. An unpaved social trail continues for approximately another 0.2 miles to an overlook. Proper footwear is recommended. Service animals are allowed, but must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet.
short_description: This short hike, with its elevated perspective and accessible trail, offers a unique view of the Little Missouri Badlands that the whole family can enjoy.

title: Visit a Lava Tube
topics: Caves, Caverns and Karst;Geology;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Volcanoes
accessibility: The trail from the parking area to the lava tube is approximately 1/4 mile long and moderately difficult, since it progresses uphill and there are many large, loose boulders along the trail. To enter into the lava tube, visitors descend a wide, sturdy ladder with handrails, then progress further into the tube by walking on and between boulders. Visitors must stoop or crawl for a distance of about 6 feet to pass under a low section of the ceiling before entering the main room of the lava tube cave.
short_description: Come explore underground in a lava tube! Around 27,000 years ago, lava flowed across the surface here. As the red-hot liquid lava stream flowed, its top cooled in the air, blackening and solidifying like a freezing creek in wintertime. The liquid lava beneath continued to flow under the solid surface, which left behind this hollow tube: frozen in time.

title: Teutonia Peak trail
accessibility: The trail is sandy and between 3 and 5 feet across. For the first 80% of the trail, it slopes gently upward at a 2% grade. At the end of the trail, it becomes much steeper as visitors climb rock steps to ascend to the top of Teutonia Peak. The views get better the higher you go, but there is no official "end" to the trail.
short_description: The Teutonia Peak Hike is a great way to examine the aftermath of the Dome Fire up close. The hike is three miles round-trip and takes between 2 and 3 hours for most people.

title: Wander Through the Joshua Trees
accessibility: Many Joshua trees can be seen from a vehicle while driving on the paved Cima Road. Visitors who wish to explore on foot may walk on the Teutonia Peak Trail (which is not accessible).
short_description: The densest concentration of Joshua trees lies along Cima Road. Although about 1/3 of the Preserve's Joshua Trees were burned during the August 2020 Dome Fire, many healthy individuals remain on Cima Road. This makes it a a wonderful spot to observe Joshua trees, icons of the Mojave Desert! Explore by car or foot. We recommend walking the Teutonia Peak trail if you want to get close to Joshua trees impacted by that fire. This area is hot during the summer, so plan ahead.

title: Hike Desert Sand Dunes
accessibility: The trail starts off level, but gets more and more difficult as hikers get closer to the summit. The views get better and better as visitors climb the dunes. Most hikers choose the top of the tallest dune as their destination, but hikers can go anywhere in the volcano field that they'd like to. No matter what path visitors choose, there is deep, soft sand at a steep uphill grade that needs to be navigated. It is not an easy trail.
short_description: Take a day hike on the Kelso Dunes! Enjoy an approximately three mile round-trip trail to the top of cream-colored dunes, formed over millennia by wind and sand. If you're lucky, you might even hear the dunes sing. This hike can be strenuous and hot. Bring water and sunscreen.

title: Watch the Award Winning Park Film - "Shiloh: Fiery Trial"
fee_description: FREE
accessibility: The movie theater is wheelchair accessible. The film is closed captioned and assistive listening devices are available. Please see a park ranger or volunteer.
short_description: A 45-minute orientation film about the Battle of Shiloh. The film shows every hour on the hour in the Shiloh visitor center.

title: Crissy Field Restored Wetlands
fee_description: Although there is no fee for this activity, the parking in the West Bluff parking and along Mason Street is paid hourly parking.
accessibility: Crissy Field Accessibility Crissy Field has accessible parking, restrooms, trails, picnicking, seasonal beach mat access, and beach wheelchairs (by request). There are two areas in Crissy Field, East Beach and West Bluff. Both areas have several accessible parking spaces. . East Beach has: An accessible restroom facility, a concrete building adjacent to the parking lot. An accessible dog washing station is also available here. An accessible picnic area for family and group picnicking. West Bluff has: Generally accessible picnic sites, an accessible Accessible restrooms near the Warming Hut There is an amphitheater that has accessible seating along the top row, here you also find an accessible picnic table Torpedo Wharf is usable, but has cracked and heaving asphalt, please proceed with caution. The Crissy Field Promenade is generally accessible and relatively flat. Beach Wheelchairs area available by reservation at least 5 days in advance. Please contact us for more information.
short_description: Walking along the Crissy Field Promenade is a great recreational activity as well as a good wildlife and sightseeing adventure.

title: Explore the park on Horseback
accessibility: The Maple Spring Trailhead has an accessible platform for mounting and dismounting horses.
short_description: Mammoth Cave National Park is an exceptional destination for anyone who loves to see the world from the back of a horse.

title: See the Stars
accessibility: Many of the paved walking trails around the visitor center and lodge can make a great place to see the night sky.
short_description: Since prehistoric times, humans have looked up at the night sky and pondered the wonders of the universe. People have used the stars and planets to navigate, keep track of time, and to connect with other cultures. Regardless of your reason, Mammoth Cave National Park provides an ideal place for stargazing.

title: Finding Flowers
accessibility: Flowers can be enjoyed at many levels. There are many places to look for wildflowers. They can be see at all pulloffs, exhibits, places and trails. Please see each location to determine the mobility needed to traverse the area. Most flowers may be gently touched and smelled, but must remain growing where they are. Please be aware that some flowers have defenses. For example, thistles have spines and poison ivy created allergic reactions. They should NOT be touched.
short_description: This is a guide to help identify what wildflowers might be blooming when in what parts of the Natchez Trace Parkway.

title: Watch the Sunrise from Derby Wharf
topics: Architecture and Building;Coasts, Islands and Atolls;Maritime;Lighthouses;Natural Sounds;Oceans;Scenic Views
accessibility: The Derby Wharf area is mostly grass which can become soft with rainfall. The beach is rocky and uneven with six adirondack chairs providing an opportunity to sit. The wharf is accessible by a flat gravel pathway that may be difficult to traverse with a wheelchair.
short_description: Enjoy an East Coast sunrise from Derby Wharf! The horizon is broad and flat, providing an expansive view of Salem Harbor.

title: Lonely Dell Ranch Historic Site
accessibility: The road leading back to Lonely Dell Ranch is a improved dirt road. Two uneven dirt trails lead down into the orchard and main ranch building areas. The orchard has a hand dug irrigation system. Feel free to walk through but watch your step. The road leading to the pioneer cemetery and Paria Canyon Wilderness trailhead are uneven and exposed to direct sun.
short_description: Hidden between the shade of trees near the muddy Paria River sits Lonely Dell Ranch. This historic site was once home to those who operated the river crossing at Lees Ferry. Life was challenging on the homestead, but the families who chose to live on this secluded outpost left behind a story of hard work and perseverance.

title: Watch Iron Works on the Saugus
topics: Architecture and Building;Colonization and Settlement;Commerce;Engineering;River and Riparian;Scenic Views;Trails
accessibility: The Saugus Iron Works Museum is fully accessible. Iron Works on the Saugus is available in English, Espanol , Deutsch , and França is.
short_description: The Saugus Iron Works official park film provides an overview of the creation, operation and historical significance of Saugus Iron Works in the 17th century.

title: Become a Saugus Iron Works B.A.R.K. Ranger
accessibility: Gravel paths weave throughout the property. The upper and lower portions of the park are relatively flat. The lower industrial portion of the site is accessible by stairs and an inclined path. There is a 0.25 mile earthen nature trail that parallels the Saugus River.
short_description: Hello four-legged friends! Do you want to explore Saugus Iron Works with your leash-holding companions? Interested in getting your very own B.A.R.K. Ranger dog tag? We made it easy for your human to help you get one. Just follow the B.A.R.K. Ranger principles!

title: Explore Manzanar Block 14 Exhibits
topics: Asian American Heritage;Japanese-American Internment;World War II
accessibility: Most exhibits are audio described. There is a sidewalk to all building entrances as well as a ramp.
short_description: Walk through one of the 36 Blocks of Manzanar to feel what life would have been like here during WWII.

title: Ride the Big Hollow Trail
accessibility: The mountain bike trail is a dirt trail with varying widths. Regular grade changes occur.
short_description: Explore the north side of the park on your mountain bike on the only mountain bike trail in the park.

title: Mammoth Cave Railroad Bike and Hike Trail
accessibility: The path is a gravel surface that may have some minor pot holes and some steep grades. The trail has a total distance of 9 miles (14.4 km).
short_description: Originally opened in 1886 the Mammoth Cave Railroad brought early tourists to Mammoth Cave and other neighboring caves in the area. Today, a portion of the path of the former Mammoth Cave Railroad has been converted into a 9-mile hike and bike trail.

title: Road Biking
accessibility: Park roads have very little paved sholders and some steep grades. We advise driving it first to asses its sutibility for your activity.
short_description: For visitors wishing to travel to Mammoth Cave National Park on two wheels instead of four, the park roadways offer miles of scenic and forested landscape to enjoy on the ride.

title: Fishing at Dinosaur National Monument
fee_description: Visitors fishing within Dinosaur National Monument must follow the fishing license requirements in accordance with the laws and regulations of the State, within whose exterior boundaries a park area or portion thereof is located. License fees may be required.
accessibility: There are no wheelchair accessible docks or piers along the Green or Yampa Rivers within the monument. The Split Mountain Boat Ramp is concrete and accessible but is limited to unloading rafts during peak hours of the day (10:00 am to 5:00 pm).
short_description: Dinosaur National Monument allows fishing as a means of providing for public enjoyment, and customary and traditional use, and regulates fishing to ensure that it is managed in a manner that avoids unacceptable impacts to park resources.

title: River Rafting at Dinosaur
topics: Canyons and Canyonlands;Geology;Night Sky;River and Riparian;Rock Landscapes and Features;Scenic Views;Wilderness
fee_description: Permit fees are required for Noncommercial River Trip Permits on rivers in Dinosaur National Monument.
accessibility: River rafting is a strenuous activity. There are no accessible facilities along the rivers. Commerical outfitters may be able to accomodate certain accessible needs.
short_description: River Rafting Information

title: Drive the Encampment Tour Route
topics: African American Heritage;American Revolution;Archeology;Architecture and Building;Sculpture;Colonization and Settlement;Commerce;Trade;Enslavement;Farming and Agriculture;Forests and Woodlands;Logging and Timber Cutting;Mills;Military;Artillery;Indigenous and Native Warrior;Infantry and Militia;US Army;Monuments and Memorials;Native American Heritage;Scenic Views;Transportation;Bridges;Roads, Routes and Highways;Wars and Conflicts;American Revolutionary War;Colonial/European Contact Conflicts;Women's History
accessibility: All tour stop locations are wheelchair accessible. The Audio Tour is available from The Encampment Store.
short_description: Drive the 10-mile Encampment Tour route and stop at nine key locations within the park. An excellent overview of the history, significance, and scenic offerings of Valley Forge National Historical Park.

title: Hike to Little Greyfield
fee_description: All visitors 16 or older must pay the park entry fee or have an America the Beautiful pass with them. Fees can be paid on the island at self-pay stations located at each dock or in person at the Mainland Visitor Center. You may also pay your entrance fee in advance online at www.pay.gov.
accessibility: The trail is a sand trail with a relatively hard packed surface. There are several sections of soft sand that can grow during dry conditions. There is little elevation change along the trail and some sections of exposed roots. Bikes are not allowed.
short_description: Take a secluded hike through the maritime forest and along the beach. This hike will take you through saw palmetto, wax myrtle and under the canopy of sprawling live oak trees. The trail will intersect with the Little Greyfield beach crossing about two miles in. Take this crossing through the dunes to a particularly isolated portion of the beach. Turn right and keep the ocean to your left to return to Sea Camp. You can also take this loop the opposite way.

title: Birding on the Beach
fee_description: All visitors 16 or older must pay the park entry fee or have an America the Beautiful pass with them. Fees can be paid on the island at self-pay stations located at each dock or in person at the Mainland Visitor Center. You may also pay your entrance fee in advance online at www.pay.gov.
accessibility: The closest beach access is 0.6 miles from the Sea Camp dock. A forested sandy path leads to the area. There are no paved surfaces. An accessible bathroom is located at the Sea Camp bathhouse. There are eight other beach crossings on the island to access the beach.
short_description: Birding on the beach can be successful in any season on Cumberland Island. There are many rear-round residents, and those around during breeding season, migrations, and winter alike. Be sure to pack your binoculars and head to the beach on your next visit to the island.

title: Walk Your Dog at Fort McHenry
fee_description: There is no fee to walk your pet at Fort McHenry because pets are not allowed in the fee area of the park.
accessibility: The park grounds are open for pets to walk. This includes grass lawns and the paved path that makes up the Sea Wall trail.
short_description: Learn about how pets can enjoy the park just as much as human visitors!

title: Watch Land of Dreams Film
topics: African American Heritage;Colonization and Settlement;Farming and Agriculture;Immigration;Native American Heritage;Westward Expansion;Homesteading
accessibility: Captions are displayed below the screen during the film. Audio description devices are availble upon request.
short_description: Watch the 23-minute film Land of Dreams: Homesteading America

title: Discover More at the Homestead Education Center
short_description: The Homestead Education Center provides you the opportunity further your knowledge about homesteading through hands-on arts and crafts, living history demonstrations, real life science experiences, and exploring farm implements.

title: Walk Main Street in Yorktown
topics: African American Heritage;American Revolution;Architecture and Building;Birthplace;Burial, Cemetery and Gravesite;Colonization and Settlement;Commerce;Trade;Enslavement;Military;Infantry and Militia;Monuments and Memorials;Religion and Spirituality;Churches;Wars and Conflicts;American Revolutionary War;Civil War
fee_description: One can walk Main street without paying the fee. To go into the Nelson House a fee is required. There is a 10 dollar fee per person, to go on the Yorktown Battlefield Tour. National Park passes are honored. Passes and tickets are available at the Yorktown Battlefield Visitor Center.
accessibility: Accessibility ● Accessible bathrooms are located at the Visitor Center and the public restrooms at Church Street.(Church Street restrooms open April 1-October 31, 2014). ● Wheelchairs are available at the visitor center on a first come first serve basis free of charge. Borrowed wheelchairs should be returned to the Visitor Center 30 minutes prior to closing. ● The Moore House, Nelson House, and Cemetery Lodge historic structures are only accessible by steps. An informational brochure is available upon request at the visitor center or at the Nelson or Moore houses. Yorktown's streets are paved, but there are few sidewalks. Main Street is closed to vehicular traffic, April through October.
short_description: Historic Yorktown is available year round. The Nelson House is open as staffing permits. There are informational waysides along Main Street.

title: Visit Theodore Roosevelt's Maltese Cross Cabin
accessibility: The Maltese Cross Cabin is accessible, with a short ramp leading into the cabin interior, though the door may be too narrow (25 inches across) to accommodate all assistive devices. Service animals are allowed, but must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet.
short_description: The Maltese Cross Cabin was Theodore Roosevelt's first home in Dakota territory. Step inside and learn about how he lived during his time in the badlands where the romance of his life began.

title: Hike The Little Mo Nature Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information .
accessibility: The Little Mo Nature Trail is approximately five feet wide and has a 0.7 mile paved inner loop and an additional 0.7 mile outer loop that has unpaved sections and steep stairs. The trail may contain uneven footing and slip or trip hazards. Proper footwear is recommended. Service animals are allowed, but must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet.
short_description: Take a short hike along the Little Mo Nature Trail and learn about the nature and geology of Theodore Roosevelt National Park!

title: Exploring the Beech Springs Nature Trail: A Quest
topics: Alligators or Crocodiles;Birds;Trails;Roads, Routes and Highways
accessibility: The entire trail is paved. In some locations the slope may slightly exceed ADA guidelines. Expect some rough spots in the pavement. The trail averages about 48" wide and has passing areas with benches. The trail is a 2800 foot loop trail.
short_description: Experience a blend of nature and civilization on the Beech Springs Nature Trail next to the Parkway Visitor Center at milepost 266. This quest, a sort of visual scavenger hunt, leads you to consider the benefits and consequences of places where nature merges with civilization. The QUESTions do not have right or wrong answers but hopefully will inspire you to learn more. If you would like additional input from a ranger, stop by the visitor center.

title: All About Hiking - Start Here!
fee_description: An entrance fee is required to get into Shenandoah National Park.
accessibility: Limberlost Trail is the only hiking trail in Shenandoah National Park that meets ADA accessibility guidelines. More information can be found in the Day Hikes section on the home page of the app.
short_description: With over 500 miles of trails in Shenandoah National Park, chances are high that you'll be lacing up your hiking boots at some point on your next trip here.

title: Watch the Theodore Roosevelt National Park Film: Refuge of the American Spirit
topics: Animals;Geology;Prairies;Native American Heritage;Presidents;River and Riparian;Rock Landscapes and Features;Buttes;Conservation Movement;Homesteading;Wilderness
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information.
accessibility: The park film is shown in the North and South Unit visitor centers, both of which are accessible. Assitive listening devices and audio description of the film are available upon request. Service animals are allowed, but must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet. More information: Accessibility in Theodore Roosevelt National Park .
short_description: Visit one of the visitor centers and watch the Theodore Roosevelt National Park film, Refuge of the American Spirit.

title: Walk Devastated Area Interpretive Trail
fee_description: There is no fee to hike the Devastated Area Trail. An entrance fee or valid pass is required to enter Lassen Volcanic National Park.
accessibility: The 0.2-mile loop is hardpacked, decomposed granite. Maximum trail grade is 5% with maximum 2% cross slope. Trail is 6 feet wide and 1,110 feet long. The trail is passable by wheelchair. Push buttons on each wayside trigger audio description through external speakers. Service animals assisting a person with a disability are permitted on the trail.
short_description: Trailside signs on this wheelchair-accessible, 0.2-mile loop provide an introduction to the 1915-1916 Lassen Peak eruption and the resulting Devastated Area.

title: Hike up Buck Hill
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information .
accessibility: Buck Hill is a steep climb up a paved trail which transitions into dirt at the top. The trail contains uneven footing, steps, and potential trip or slip hazards. Proper footwear is recommended. Service animals are allowed, but must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet.
short_description: Hike to the top of Buck Hill, one of the highest points in the park, and get an amazing 360° view of the surrounding badlands!

title: Stargaze in Shenandoah
fee_description: An entrance fee is required to get into Shenandoah National Park.
accessibility: Night skies can be viewed from any location in the Park. Big Meadows is an easily accessible location with a paved parking lot.
short_description: Shenandoah National Park has distinctly accessible night skies that make stargazing and astrophotography a fun and insightful activity for all ages.

title: Hike to the Top of Big Kennesaw Mountain
fee_description: Kennesaw Mountain National Battlefield Park does charge an entrance fee. It is $5 a day or $40 a year, and National Park's passes are available. This fee is charged as you park in any of the designated parking lots. The Visitor Center lot is how you access the Kennesaw Mountain trail and is subject to parking fee enforcement. For more information on the Kennesaw Mountain's fees, please see link here.
accessibility: The trail to the top of Big Kennesaw Mountain is not accessible to all visitors, specifically those in need of wheelchairs or that have trouble walking long distances (over a mile). The marjority of the trail is dirt, and it can be rocky and steep in some areas. However, we do have a two-lane, paved road that can also be used to access the parking lot at the top of the mountain. This road is usually open to personal vehicles from Monday - Friday, 6:30 am to 5:00 pm from November to March, or 6:30 am to 7:00 pm March to November (weather pending). The road is closed to personal vehicles Saturday and Sunday. Please also keep in mind that the road takes you to the parking lot at the peak of the mountain. To get to the peak, you must still ascend the set of stairs on the stone viewing station.
short_description: This 1.1 mile hike to the summit of Big Kennesaw mountain is one of the most scenic and popular trails in the park. You will see Confederate trenches and artillery positions, as well as breathtaking views of the surrounding area. It is moderately difficult and closed toed shoes and plenty of water are recommended.

title: Go Birdwatching in Shenandoah
accessibility: The accessibility of an area depends on where you choose to birdwatch.
short_description: Birdwatching is a fun activity that the whole family can enjoy, and Shenandoah provides the perfect habitat to spot a variety of different species, including those colorful, neotropical migratory birds!

title: Shop at the Bookstore
time_of_day: Open daily from 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM (closed Christmas Day).
accessibility: The bookstore is located on the second floor of the Cumberland Island National Seashore Visitor Center. Stairs lead upstairs. There is an elevator entrance as well from the street level. No pets, except service animals, are allowed in the building.
short_description: Stop by the bookstore at Cumberland Island’s Visitor Center in Saint Marys, GA, open daily from 8:00 AM – 4:00 PM (closed Christmas Day). You will find books related to the island’s natural and cultural history, apparel, postcards, pins, patches, magnets, and more.

title: Visit the National Cemetery
accessibility: The cemetery is wheelchair accessible. Wheelchairs are available for loan at the park visitor center.
short_description: Explore the Shiloh National Cemetery.

title: Earn Your Corinth Junior Ranger Badge
topics: African American Heritage;Military;Artillery;Battlefields;Cavalry;Infantry and Militia;US Army;Reconstruction;Trains and Railroads;Wars and Conflicts;Civil War
fee_description: FREE
accessibility: The Center, exhibits, and restrooms are wheelchair accessible.
short_description: The Corinth Civil War Interpretive Center Junior Ranger Program. Earn your badge and certficate today!

title: Walk Lily Pond Interpretive Trail
topics: Coniferous Forests;Freshwater Springs;Lakes;Mountains;Rock Landscapes and Features;Trails;Volcanoes
fee_description: There is no fee to walk the Lily Pond Interpretive Trail. An entrance fee or valid pass is required to enter Lassen Volcanic National Park.
accessibility: The composition of the trail is dirt and rock. Most of the trail is flat with the exception of two short, steep areas. There is one footbridge crossing. Service animals assisting a person with a disability are permitted on park trails. A service animal, as described by the ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) performs a specific task for a disabled person.
short_description: A half-mile, self-led, interpretive loop explores the rich diversity of plant and animal life in the Manzanita Lake Area.

title: Walk Manzanita Lake Trail
fee_description: There is no fee to walk Manzanita Lake Trail. An entrance fee or valid pass is required to enter Lassen Volcanic National Park.
accessibility: The trail is not recommended for wheelchair use. The trail is narrow in places with numerous obstacles including tree roots and exposed rocks. Individuals in wheelchairs can access the Manzanita Lake Picnic Area/Boat Launch to enjoy lake access, bird watching, wildlife viewing, and sunset watching. Service animals assisting a person with a disability are permitted on park trails. A service animal, as described by the ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) performs a specific task for a disabled person.
short_description: Manzanita Lake Trail is an easy, mostly flat walk suitable for families with young children. It is not stroller-friendly. The walk offers scenic views of Lassen Peak and Chaos Crags volcanoes and birding and wildlife watching opportunities. The trail is popular for sunset viewing.

title: Walk the Anhinga Trail
fee_description: Entrance fees may apply, see Fees & Passes information .
accessibility: The Anhinga Trail is paved cement and wooden boardwalk. It is wheelchair and stroller accessible. It is flat, free of rough terrain and between 4-8 feet wide. Pets are not allowed on the Anhinga Trail with the exception of service animals
short_description: The famous Anhinga Trail is a self-guided pavement and boardwalk trail winding through and over sawgrass marsh and freshwater slough. A paved path leads you along the water and to a looping boardwalk, providing views into the prairie and the clear waters of the slough. You may see alligators, fish, turtles, anhingas, and many other birds, especially during the winter, when the generally lower waters of the dry season concentrate aquatic wildlife in the slough.

title: Drive the Essex Coastal Scenic Byway
topics: African American Heritage;American Revolution;Animals;Birds;Architecture and Building;Arts;Photography;Poetry and Literature;Burial, Cemetery and Gravesite;Climate Change;Coasts, Islands and Atolls;Enslavement;Hispanic American Heritage;Immigration;LGB American Heritage;Latino American Heritage;Maritime;Migrations;Military;Monuments and Memorials;Native American Heritage;Natural Sounds;Oceans;Scenic Views;Roads, Routes and Highways;Urban America;American Revolutionary War;Civil War
accessibility: This activity is primarily experienced from your vehicle. Accessibility will vary based on stops and the specifics of locations. National Historic Site locations are fully accessible for limited mobility and wheelchairs.
short_description: Discover 90 miles of New England coastal life passing through Essex National Heritage Area and Salem Maritime National Historic Site.

title: Look for Red-Legged Frogs in Mori Point
accessibility: Old Mori Trail Overview Distance: 1.0 mi (1.6 km) Elevation Gain: 30 ft Time: 1 hour Trailhead: Mori Point Slope: Avg -1% Max 5% Side Slope: Avg 3% Max 9% Width: Avg 125" Min 86" Trail Surface: Firm Safety - Stay on the established trail. Keep an eye out for poison oak. - Observe warning signs and railings-these exist for your safety. Cliffs along the bluffs can be unstable and hazardous. - Dress in layers and be prepared for varying weather conditions. Sunny days along the coast can turn windy, foggy, and cold very fast. Parking There is trailhead parking at Mori Point including two ADA accessible spots. Parking is limited. If you park in the nearby streets, please observe parking regulations.
short_description: Watch for California's red-legged frogs in the restored pond habitat at Mori Point.

title: Wildflower Walk at Fort Funston
accessibility: Sunset Trail Accessibility Overview Distance: 1.5 mi (2.8 km) Time: 1 hour Trailhead: Sunset Trail Slope: Avg 6%, Max 27% Side Slope: Avg 3%, Max 8% Width: Avg 87 in., Min 40 in. Trail Surface: Firm Safety - Stay on the established trail. Keep an eye out for poison oak. - Observe warning signs and railings-these exist for your safety. - Dress in layers and be prepared for varying weather conditions. Sunny days along the coast can turn windy, foggy, and cold very fast. - Do not climb on the coastal bluffs or edges, the sand and rocks are loose and eroding and dangerous! - People have fallen from these cliffs -- and died! Parking There is parking at Fort Funston, including ADA accessible parking. Bathrooms Bathrooms are located near the parking area.
short_description: Take a walk and enjoy the scenic views of the wildflowers blooming at Fort Funston.

title: Watch the Film "Corinth Crossroads: A Town Amidst War"
fee_description: FREE
accessibility: Parking area, museum, and theater are accessible. The film is closed-captioned and assistant listening devices are available on request.
short_description: The film shows on the hour and half-hour everyday at The Corinth Civil War Interpretive Center.

title: Visit and Explore the Corinth Civil War Intepretive Center
topics: Enslavement;Military;Artillery;Battlefields;Cavalry;Infantry and Militia;Monuments and Memorials;Wars and Conflicts;Civil War
fee_description: No fees.
accessibility: Parking, museum, and restrooms accessible.
short_description: Museum exhibits include artifacts, interactive displays, and multimedia presentations.

title: Hike the Shiloh Indian Mounds Complex
accessibility: Accessible parking.
short_description: An easy 1.1 mile interpretive trail with 13 wayside exhibits explores this pre-historic village.

title: Bike the South Unit Scenic Drive
fee_description: Access to the scenic drive requires payment of an entrance fee or possession of an NPS pass. Refer to 'Fees & Passes' for prices.
accessibility: The scenic drive is a two-lane, paved road. Accessible parking is available at most paved parking lots and pull-outs, though bike racks may not be. There are two accessible trails available: Skyline Vista and Boicourt Overlook. Service animals are allowed, but must be on a leash no longer than 6 feet. title: Bike the Cowboy Trail
duration:
Visitors can spend as much time as they prefer on the Cowboy Trail. 

Biking to the historic railroad bridge from the Valentine City Park Trailhead is 2.5 miles, one way.

Walking out and back to the historic railroad bridge from the Highway 20 Trailhead and parking lot can take about an hour, but can be done in much shorter time as well. The distance to the bridge from that trailhead is 0.75 miles.

title: Float the Niobrara River

(If Smith Falls is just a pit-stop while you float and you are not pulling out there, just stopping to see the falls, then a pass is not required because you are not accessing the parking areas by vehicle.) Other public access launch/landing sites along the Niobrara National Scenic River do not require fees. Private Launch/Landing Locations: There are many privately owned launch and landing sites on the Niobrara NSR managed by those who own the land along the river. These can be accessed by working with our local River Outfitters to arrange launch and landing access, shuttles, equipment rentals, and pick-ups. Fees vary by ownership for these sites.
accessibility: Fort Niobrara National Wildlife Refuge has one handicap accessible canoe, kayak, or tube launch. It is located on the North side of the Cornell Bridge on the way to the Burr Oak Picnic Area. It has its own parking lot. We recommend contacting the Fort Niobrara National Wildlife Refuge for more information about this launch site. NOTE: There are no other designated handicap accessible canoe, kayak, or tube landings/launches further down river.
short_description: Experience the beauty of the Niobrara National Scenic River up close and personal by floating the gentle waters through six ecosystems, past waterfalls, and under historic bridges. A gem in the Sandhills of the Great Plains.

At the top of the hill is an information panel about the Rio Grande. Service dogs are allowed on this trail.
